title.raw: 卷2 太祖紀 Volume 2 Annals: Taizu (Emperor Daowu)

sentences.zh: 太祖道武皇帝，諱珪，昭成皇帝之嫡孫，獻明皇帝之子也。

translations.literal: The Taizu, Emperor Daowu — taboo name Gui — was the eldest son's son of Emperor Zhaocheng and the son of Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, Emperor Daowu, bore the taboo name Gui. He was a grandson of Emperor Zhaocheng by the principal line and the son of Emperor Xianming.

sentences.zh: 母曰獻明賀皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was called Empress He of Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress He of Xianming.

sentences.zh: 初因遷徙，遊于雲澤，既而寢息，夢日出室內，寤而見光自牖屬天，歘然有感。

translations.literal: At first, because of migration, she traveled at Yunze; later she lay down to rest, dreamed the sun came forth inside the chamber, awoke and saw light from the window reaching heaven, and suddenly felt stirred.
translations.idiomatic: During the migrations she had been traveling in Yunze. One day she lay down to sleep and dreamed the sun rose within her chamber; when she woke, light poured from the window to the sky, and she was seized by a sudden presentiment.

sentences.zh: 以建國三十四年七月七日，生太祖於參合陂北，其夜復有光明。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month in the thirty-fourth year of Jianguo, the Taizu was born north of Canhebo; that night again there was radiance.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month in the thirty-fourth year of Jianguo, the future Taizu was born north of Canhebo, and that night bright light shone again.

sentences.zh: 昭成大悅，羣臣稱慶，大赦，告於祖宗。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng was greatly pleased; the host of officials offered congratulations; a general amnesty was proclaimed; announcement was made to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaocheng rejoiced; his ministers celebrated; the realm was granted amnesty; and the birth was reported to the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 保者以帝體重倍於常兒，竊獨奇怪。

translations.literal: The nurse found the emperor's body weight twice that of ordinary infants; she alone marveled at it in secret.
translations.idiomatic: His nurse found the infant twice as heavy as other children and kept her wonder to herself.

sentences.zh: 明年有榆生於埋胞之坎，後遂成林。

translations.literal: The next year an elm grew at the pit where the afterbirth had been buried; afterward it became a forest.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an elm sprouted where his afterbirth had been buried, and in time the saplings grew into a wood.

sentences.zh: 弱而能言，目有光曜，廣顙大耳，眾咸異之。

translations.literal: Though young he could speak; his eyes had bright light; broad forehead and large ears; the multitude all regarded him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke while still a child; his eyes shone; his forehead was broad and his ears large, and all who saw him thought him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，昭成崩。

translations.literal: At age six, Zhaocheng died.
translations.idiomatic: When he was six, Emperor Zhaocheng died.

sentences.zh: 苻堅遣將內侮，將遷帝於長安，既而獲免。

translations.literal: Fu Jian sent generals to invade within the borders; they were about to move the emperor to Chang'an; afterward he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent armies against the realm and planned to relocate the boy to Chang'an, but in the end he was spared.

sentences.zh: 語在燕鳳傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Yan Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Yan Feng.

sentences.zh: 堅軍既還，國眾離散。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's army having returned, the state's people scattered.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's forces withdrew, the tribes of the state broke apart.

sentences.zh: 堅使劉庫仁、劉衞辰分攝國事。

translations.literal: Fu Jian had Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen separately take charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian set Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen to govern the tribes between them.

sentences.zh: 南部大人長孫嵩及元他等，盡將故民南依庫仁，帝於是轉幸獨孤部。

translations.literal: The southern grandee Zhangsun Song and Yuan Ta and others all led the former people south to attach to Kuren; the emperor then turned and took refuge with the Dugu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Song, the southern chieftain, Yuan Ta, and others led the old followers south to Liu Kuren, while the future emperor withdrew to the Dugu tribe.

sentences.zh: 元年，葬昭成皇帝於金陵，營梓宮，木柹盡生成林。

translations.literal: Year 1: buried Emperor Zhaocheng at Jinling and built the imperial coffin palace; the wooden pegs all grew and became a forest.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year Emperor Zhaocheng was buried at Jinling. While the imperial tomb was being built, every coffin peg put in the ground took root until a grove stood on the mound.

sentences.zh: 帝雖沖幼，而嶷然不羣。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was young and tender, he stood apart from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a child, he already carried himself apart from other boys.

sentences.zh: 庫仁常謂其子曰：帝有高天下之志，興復洪業，光揚祖宗者，必此主也。

translations.literal: Kuren often told his sons: The emperor has the will to take all under Heaven; to raise again great enterprise and spread light on the ancestors — it must be this lord.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren often told his sons, "That boy intends to rule the world, restore our great undertaking, and glorify the ancestors. The throne will be his."

sentences.zh: 七年，冬十月，[1]苻堅敗于淮南。

translations.literal: Year 7, winter, tenth month, [1] Fu Jian was defeated at Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, in the tenth month of winter, [1] Fu Jian was defeated at Huainan.

sentences.zh: 是月，慕容文等殺庫仁，庫仁弟眷攝國部。

translations.literal: That month, Murong Wen and others killed Kuren; Kuren's younger brother Juan took charge of the state's tribes.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Murong Wen and his party killed Liu Kuren, and Kuren's younger brother Juan assumed leadership of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 八年，慕容暐弟沖僭立。

translations.literal: Year 8: Murong Wei's younger brother Chong set himself up in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Murong Chong, younger brother of Murong Wei, declared himself ruler in defiance of the court.

sentences.zh: 姚萇自稱大單于、萬年秦王。

translations.literal: Yao Chang styled himself Great Chanyu and Ten-Thousand-Year King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang took the titles Great Chanyu and King of Qin of the Ten Thousand Years.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂僭稱燕王。

translations.literal: Murong Chui presumptively styled himself King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui presumptuously declared himself King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 九年，庫仁子顯殺眷而代之，乃將謀逆。

translations.literal: Year 9: Kuren's son Xian killed Juan and replaced him; then he plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Liu Kuren's son Xian murdered Juan and seized his place, then began to plot treason against the emperor.

sentences.zh: 商人王霸知之，履帝足於眾中，帝乃馳還。

translations.literal: The merchant Wang Ba knew of it; he trod on the emperor's foot in the crowd; the emperor then galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: A trader named Wang Ba learned of the plot and, in the press of the crowd, stepped on the emperor's foot; the emperor understood and rode away at once.

sentences.zh: 是時故大人梁蓋盆子六眷，為顯謀主，盡知其計，密使部人穆崇馳告。

translations.literal: At that time the former grandee Liang Gaizi's son Liu Juan was Xian's chief plotter; he knew the whole plan and secretly sent a tribesman, Mu Chong, to ride and report.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Juan, son of the former chieftain Liang Gaizi, was Xian's chief conspirator. He knew every detail and secretly sent Mu Chong of his following to gallop ahead with warning.

sentences.zh: 帝乃陰結舊臣長孫犍、元他等。

translations.literal: The emperor then secretly allied with old ministers Zhangsun Jian, Yuan Ta, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then bound his old supporters Zhangsun Jian, Yuan Ta, and the rest in a secret league.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，乃幸賀蘭部。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: then he took refuge with the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he withdrew to the Helan tribe.

sentences.zh: 其日，顯果使人求帝，不及。

translations.literal: That day Xian indeed sent men seeking the emperor but did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Xian sent men to seize the emperor, but they arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 語在獻明太后傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of the Empress Dowager Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of the Empress Dowager Xianming.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鮮卑乞伏國仁私署大單于。

translations.literal: That year the Xianbei Qifu Guoren privately styled himself Great Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Xianbei leader Qifu Guoren privately took the title Great Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 苻堅為姚萇所殺，子丕僭立。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang; his son Pi set himself up in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang, and his son Fu Pi declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 登國元年春正月戊申，帝即代王位，郊天，建元，大會於牛川。

translations.literal: Dengguo year 1, spring, first month, day wushen: the emperor assumed the kingship of Dai, worshipped Heaven, established the era name, and held a great assembly at Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dengguo, on the wushen day of the first month of spring, he took the throne as King of Dai, sacrificed to Heaven, proclaimed the new reign, and held a great gathering at Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 復以長孫嵩為南部大人，以叔孫普洛為北部大人。

translations.literal: Again appointed Zhangsun Song as southern grandee and Shusun Puluo as northern grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He reappointed Zhangsun Song as southern chieftain and Shusun Puluo as northern chieftain.

sentences.zh: 班爵叙勳，各有差。

translations.literal: Distributed ranks and ordered exploits — each had his grade.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked the nobles and recorded their merits, assigning each his due reward.

sentences.zh: 二月，幸定襄之盛樂。

translations.literal: Second month: visited Shengle in Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he went to Shengle in Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 息眾課農。

translations.literal: Let the people rest and assessed agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the people respite from war and set them to farming.

sentences.zh: 三月，劉顯自善無南走馬邑，其族奴真率所部來降。

translations.literal: Third month: Liu Xian himself fled south from Shanyou to Mayi; his tribesman Nuzhen led his following to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Liu Xian fled south from Shanyou toward Mayi, while his kinsman Nuzhen brought their clans in submission.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，改稱魏王。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: changed title to Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he changed his title to Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 五月，車駕東幸陵石。

translations.literal: Fifth month: the imperial carriage went east to Lingshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the court traveled east to Lingshi.

sentences.zh: 護佛侯部帥侯辰、乙弗部帥代題叛走。

translations.literal: The chief of the Protect-Buddha Marquis tribe, Hou Chen, and the chief of the Yifu tribe, Dai Ti, rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Chen, chief of the Hubohou tribe, and Dai Ti, chief of the Yifu, rose in revolt and fled.

sentences.zh: 諸將追之，帝曰：「侯辰等世修職役，雖有小愆，宜且忍之。

translations.literal: The generals pursued them. The emperor said: "Hou Chen and the others for generations have performed their duties; though they have small faults, we should for the moment bear with them.
translations.idiomatic: His officers asked leave to pursue them. The emperor said, "Hou Chen and his people have served for generations. Their offense is slight; for now we should endure it.

sentences.zh: 當今草創，人情未一，愚近者固應趑趄，不足追也。」

translations.literal: Now at the founding, hearts are not yet one; the foolish and near at hand should indeed hesitate — not worth pursuing."
translations.idiomatic: We are only beginning to build the state, and loyalty is not yet settled. The timid will hang back — there is no need to chase them."

sentences.zh: 秋七月己酉，車駕還盛樂。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiyou: the imperial carriage returned to Shengle.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jiyou, the court returned to Shengle.

sentences.zh: 代題復以部落來降，旬有數日，亡奔劉顯。

translations.literal: Dai Ti again came with his tribe to surrender; after several tens of days he fled and ran to Liu Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ti submitted again with his tribe, but within a fortnight he broke away and fled to Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 帝使其孫倍斤代領部落。

translations.literal: The emperor had his grandson Beijin take charge of the tribe in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set his grandson Beijin over Dai Ti's people.

sentences.zh: 是月，劉顯弟肺泥率騎掠奴真部落，[2]既而率以來降。

translations.literal: That month, Liu Xian's younger brother Feini led horsemen to plunder Nuzhen's tribe, [2] and afterward led them in to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Xian's brother Feini raided Nuzhen's camp with cavalry, [2] then brought his own followers in to submit.

sentences.zh: 初，帝叔父窟咄為苻堅徙于長安，因隨慕容永，永以為新興太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor's uncle Kudou had been moved by Fu Jian to Chang'an; he followed Murong Yong, and Yong made him administrator of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor's uncle Kudou had been relocated to Chang'an by Fu Jian. He later followed Murong Yong, who appointed him administrator of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 八月，劉顯遣弟亢泥迎窟咄，以兵隨之，來逼南境。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Liu Xian sent his younger brother Kangni to welcome Kudou, with troops following, coming to press the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Xian sent his brother Kangni to escort Kudou south at the head of an army that threatened the frontier.

sentences.zh: 於是諸部騷動，人心顧望。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribes were disturbed and men's hearts wavered.
translations.idiomatic: At once the tribes stirred and loyalty wavered.

sentences.zh: 帝左右于桓等，[3]與諸部人謀為逆以應之。

translations.literal: At the emperor's side, Yu Huan and others, [3] with men of the tribes plotted rebellion to answer them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan and others close to the emperor [3] conspired with tribal leaders to join the rebels.

sentences.zh: 事泄，誅造謀者五人，餘悉不問。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; five plotters were executed; the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered. Five ringleaders were put to death; the rest were not punished.

sentences.zh: 帝慮內難，乃北踰陰山，幸賀蘭部，阻山為固。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing internal trouble, then crossed north over the Yin Mountains and took refuge with the Helan tribe, blocking the mountains for security.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing civil war, he crossed the Yin Mountains to the north, withdrew to the Helan tribe, and held the passes for defense.

sentences.zh: 遣行人安同、長孫賀使于慕容垂以徵師，垂遣使朝貢，并令其子賀驎帥步騎以隨同等。

translations.literal: He sent the envoy An Tong and Zhangsun He as envoys to Murong Chui to request troops; Chui sent envoys with tribute and ordered his son Helin to lead foot and horse to follow An Tong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched An Tong and Zhangsun He to Murong Chui to ask for aid. Chui sent tribute in return and ordered his son Helin to march with infantry and cavalry in support.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，賀驎軍未至而寇已前逼，於是北部大人叔孫普洛等十三人及諸烏丸亡奔衞辰。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Helin's army had not yet arrived when the enemy had already pressed forward; thereupon the northern grandee Shusun Puluo and thirteen others and various Wuhuan fled to Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, before Helin's troops arrived, the rebels were already closing in. Shusun Puluo, the northern chieftain, twelve other leaders, and many Wuhuan bands fled to Liu Weichen.

sentences.zh: 帝自弩山遷幸牛川，屯于延水南，出代谷，會賀驎於高柳，大破窟咄。

translations.literal: The emperor moved from Nushan to Niuchuan, encamped south of the Yanshui, went out through Daigu, and joined Helin at Gaoliu; Kudou was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew from Nushan to Niuchuan, camped south of the Yanshui, marched out through Daigu, and met Helin at Gaoliu, where Kudou's forces were shattered.

sentences.zh: 窟咄奔衞辰，衞辰殺之，帝悉收其眾。

translations.literal: Kudou fled to Weichen; Weichen killed him; the emperor gathered in all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Kudou fled to Liu Weichen, who killed him; the emperor absorbed his entire following.

sentences.zh: 十二月，慕容垂遣使朝貢，奉帝西單于印綬，封上谷王。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute, presenting the seal and cord of Western Chanyu and enfeoffing him as Prince of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute, offering the seal of Western Chanyu and investing him as Prince of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused the honors.

sentences.zh: 是歲，慕容垂僭稱皇帝於中山，自號大燕。

translations.literal: That year Murong Chui presumptively styled himself emperor at Zhongshan, taking the era name Great Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Chui declared himself emperor at Zhongshan under the title Great Yan.

sentences.zh: 苻丕死，苻登自立於隴東。

translations.literal: Fu Pi died; Fu Deng set himself up in Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi died, and Fu Deng established himself in Longdong.

sentences.zh: 姚萇稱皇帝於長安，自號大秦。

translations.literal: Yao Chang styled himself emperor at Chang'an, taking the era name Great Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang proclaimed himself emperor at Chang'an under the title Great Qin.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖為部下所殺。

translations.literal: Murong Chong was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong was murdered by his own officers.

sentences.zh: 慕容永僭立。

translations.literal: Murong Yong set himself up in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong rose in rebellion and claimed the throne.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，班賜功臣長孫嵩等七十三人各有差。

translations.literal: Year 2, spring, first month: distributed rewards to meritorious ministers Zhangsun Song and seventy-two others, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, in the first month of spring, he rewarded Zhangsun Song and seventy-two other meritorious men, each in proportion to his service.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝幸寧川。

translations.literal: Second month: the emperor visited Ningchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor went to Ningchuan.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，遣行人安同徵兵於慕容垂，垂使子賀驎率眾來會。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: sent the envoy An Tong to levy troops from Murong Chui; Chui sent his son Helin to lead the host to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he sent An Tong to Murong Chui to raise troops; Chui sent Helin at the head of an army to rendezvous with him.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝親征劉顯於馬邑南，追至彌澤，大破之，顯南奔慕容永，盡收其部落。

translations.literal: Sixth month: the emperor personally campaigned against Liu Xian south of Mayi, pursued to Mize, greatly defeated him; Xian fled south to Murong Yong; all his tribes were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor marched in person against Liu Xian south of Mayi, chased him to Mize, and routed him utterly. Xian fled south to Murong Yong, and the emperor absorbed every clan that had followed him.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，帝至自伐顯。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: the emperor returned from the campaign against Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he returned from the expedition against Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸卯，幸濡源，遣外朝大人王建使於慕容垂。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guimao: visited Ruyuan; sent the outer-court grandee Wang Jian as envoy to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day guimao, he went to Ruyuan and dispatched Wang Jian, a senior minister of the outer court, as envoy to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遂幸赤城。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: then visited Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he proceeded to Chicheng.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，巡松漠，還幸牛川。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: toured Songmo; returned and visited Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he toured Songmo, then returned to Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 三年春二月，帝東巡。

translations.literal: Year 3, second month of spring: the emperor toured east.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, in the second month of spring, he made an eastern progress.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，幸東赤城。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: visited East Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he went to East Chicheng.

sentences.zh: 五月癸亥，北征庫莫奚。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day guihai: northern expedition against the Kumo Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the fifth month he marched north against the Kumo Xi.

sentences.zh: 六月，大破之，獲其四部雜畜十餘萬，渡弱落水。

translations.literal: Sixth month: greatly defeated them; captured mixed livestock of their four divisions numbering more than a hundred thousand; crossed the Ruoluo River.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he crushed them, seized more than a hundred thousand head of mixed herds from their four divisions, and crossed the Ruoluo River.

sentences.zh: 班賞將士各有差。

translations.literal: Distributed rewards to officers and soldiers, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded officers and soldiers according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚申，庫莫部帥鳩集遺散，[4]夜犯行宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen: the Kumo chief Juji gathered the scattered, [4] and by night attacked the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the seventh month of autumn, Juji, a Kumo chieftain, rallied the fugitives [4] and struck the imperial camp by night.

sentences.zh: 縱騎撲討，盡殺之。

translations.literal: He loosed cavalry to strike and pursue; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent horsemen in pursuit and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 其月，帝還赤城。

translations.literal: That month the emperor returned to Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: That month he returned to Chicheng.

sentences.zh: 八月，使九原公元儀使於慕容垂。

translations.literal: Eighth month: sent Jiuyuan Prince Yuan Yi as envoy to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent Prince Yuan Yi of Jiuyuan as envoy to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，慕容垂遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Murong Chui sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十有二月辛卯，車駕西征，至女水，討解如部，大破之，獲男女雜畜十餘萬。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day xinmao: the imperial carriage campaigned west, reached Nüshui, attacked the Jieru tribe, greatly defeated them, and captured men and women and mixed livestock numbering more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the twelfth month he marched west to the Nüshui, struck the Jieru tribe, broke them completely, and took more than a hundred thousand captives and mixed herds.

sentences.zh: 是歲，乞伏國仁死，弟乾歸立，私署河南王。

translations.literal: That year Qifu Guoren died; his younger brother Qian'gui succeeded him and privately styled himself Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qifu Guoren died. His younger brother Qifu Qiangui succeeded him and privately took the title Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月甲寅，襲高車諸部落，大破之。

translations.literal: Year 4, spring, first month, day jiayin: raided the Gaoche tribes, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the jiayin day of the first month of spring, he raided the Gaoche tribes and routed them.

sentences.zh: 二月癸巳，至女水，討叱突隣部，大破之。

translations.literal: Second month, day guisi: reached Nüshui and attacked the Chituolin tribe, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the second month he reached the Nüshui and defeated the Chituolin tribe.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，賀染干兄弟率諸部來救，與大軍相遇，逆擊走之。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Herangan and his brothers led the tribes to the rescue; they met the great army; he struck them in reverse and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day Herangan and his brothers marched to relieve the enemy, met the main force, and were beaten back in a counterattack.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，行還赤城。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: on the march returned to Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he returned to Chicheng on the march.

sentences.zh: 五月，陳留公元虔使於慕容垂。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian was sent as envoy to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he sent Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu as envoy to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，垂遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Chui sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Murong Chui again sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，氐呂光自稱三河王，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year the Di leader Lü Guang styled himself Prince of the Three Rivers and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Di chieftain Lü Guang declared himself Prince of the Three Rivers and sent tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 五年春三月甲申，帝西征，次鹿渾海，襲高車袁紇部，大破之，虜獲生口、馬牛羊二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Year 5, spring, third month, day jiashen: the emperor campaigned west, halted at Luhunhai, raided the Gaoche Yuanhe division, greatly defeated them, and captured living captives, horses, cattle, and sheep numbering more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on the jiashen day of the third month of spring, he marched west to Luhunhai, fell on the Gaoche Yuanhe division, shattered it, and took more than two hundred thousand people and animals.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂遣子賀驎率眾來會。

translations.literal: Murong Chui sent his son Helin to lead the host to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui sent Helin with an army to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙寅，行幸意辛山，與賀驎討賀蘭、紇突隣、紇奚諸部落，大破之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingyin: on the march visited Yixinshan; with Helin attacked the Helan, Ketulin, and Kexi tribes, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the fourth month of summer he advanced to Yixinshan, and with Helin crushed the Helan, Ketulin, and Kexi tribes.

sentences.zh: 六月，還幸牛川。

translations.literal: Sixth month: returned and visited Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he returned to Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 衞辰遣子直力鞮寇賀蘭部，圍之。

translations.literal: Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi to raid the Helan tribe and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi to attack the Helan and besieged them.

sentences.zh: 賀訥等請降，告困。

translations.literal: He Ne and others asked to surrender and reported their distress.
translations.idiomatic: He Ne and the other Helan leaders begged to submit and sent word that they were hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙子，帝引兵救之，至羊山，直力鞮退走。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day bingzi: the emperor led troops to the rescue; reached Yangshan; Zhiligidi withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the seventh month of autumn the emperor marched to relieve them. When he reached Yangshan, Zhiligidi broke off and fled.

sentences.zh: 八月，還幸牛川。

translations.literal: Eighth month: returned and visited Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he returned again to Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 遣秦王觚使於慕容垂。

translations.literal: Sent Prince Gu of Qin as envoy to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Prince Gu of Qin as envoy to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 九月壬申，討叱奴部於囊曲河，大破之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day renshen: attacked the Chinu tribe at Nangqu River, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the ninth month he attacked the Chinu at the Nangqu River and defeated them utterly.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，遷雲中，討高車豆陳部於狼山，破之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: moved to Yunzhong, attacked the Gaoche Douchen division at Langshan, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he moved the court to Yunzhong, struck the Gaoche Douchen at Langshan, and broke them.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，紇奚部大人庫寒舉部內屬。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Kuhan, grandee of the Hexi tribe, led his tribe to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Kuhan, chieftain of the Hexi, brought his people in submission.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，紇突隣大人屈地鞬舉部內屬。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Qudijian, grandee of the Hetulin tribe, led his tribe to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Qudijian, chieftain of the Hetulin, led his clan to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝還次白漠。

translations.literal: The emperor returned and halted at Baimo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew and encamped at Baimo.

sentences.zh: 六年春二月，幸紐垤川。

translations.literal: Year 6, spring, second month: visited Niudichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, in the second month of spring, he went to Niudichuan.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣九原公元儀、陳留公元虔等西討黜弗部，大破之。

translations.literal: Third month: sent Jiuyuan Prince Yuan Yi, Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian, and others west to attack the Chufu tribe, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he sent Prince Yuan Yi of Jiuyuan and Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu west against the Chufu and routed them.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，祠天。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: sacrificed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he offered sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 六月，慕容賀驎破賀訥於赤城。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Murong Helin defeated He Ne at Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Murong Helin defeated He Ne at Chicheng.

sentences.zh: 帝引兵救之，驎退走。

translations.literal: The emperor led troops to rescue him; Helin withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched to his relief; Helin broke off and fled.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬申，講武於牛川，行還紐垤川。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day renshen: conducted martial exercises at Niuchuan, then on the march returned to Niudichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the seventh month of autumn he held a military review at Niuchuan, then returned to Niudichuan.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂止元觚而求名馬，帝絕之。

translations.literal: Murong Chui detained Yuan Gu and demanded famous horses; the emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui held Yuan Gu hostage and demanded prized horses; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使於慕容永，永使其大鴻臚慕容鈞奉表勸進尊號。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to Murong Yong; Yong had his Grand Herald Murong Jun present a memorial urging assumption of the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to Murong Yong, who had his Grand Herald Murong Jun submit a memorial urging him to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 其月，衞辰遣子直力鞮出棝楊塞，侵及黑城。

translations.literal: That month, Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi out from Puyang Pass, invading as far as Heicheng.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi through Puyang Pass to raid as far as Heicheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝襲五原，屠之。

translations.literal: Ninth month: the emperor raided Wuyuan and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he stormed Wuyuan and put the city to the sword.

sentences.zh: 收其積穀，還紐垤川。

translations.literal: Collected their stored grain and returned to Niudichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He seized their granaries and withdrew to Niudichuan.

sentences.zh: 於棝楊塞北，樹碑記功。

translations.literal: North of Puyang Pass, erected a stele recording merit.
translations.idiomatic: North of Puyang Pass he raised a stele to commemorate the victory.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊戌，北征蠕蠕，追之，及於大磧南牀山下，大破之，班賜從臣各有差。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuxu: northern campaign against the Rouran, pursued them, caught up south of the great desert below South Bed Mountain, greatly defeated them, distributed rewards to accompanying ministers each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the tenth month of winter he marched north against the Rouran, pursued them to South Bed Mountain south of the great desert, crushed them, and rewarded his officers by rank.

sentences.zh: 其東西二部主匹候跋及縕紇提，[5]斬別帥屋擊于。

translations.literal: The eastern and western division leaders Pihouba and Wenheti, [5] beheaded the separate commander Wujiyu.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs of the eastern and western wings, Pihouba and Wenheti, [5] cut down the sub-commander Wujiyu.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set out in the Rouran biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 十有一月戊辰，還幸紐垤川。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day wuchen: returned and visited Niudichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the eleventh month he returned to Niudichuan.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，衞辰遣子直力鞮寇南部。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Weichen sent his son Zhiligidi to raid the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day Weichen sent Zhiligidi to attack the southern marches.

sentences.zh: 己卯，車駕出討。

translations.literal: On day jimao, the imperial carriage set out on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day the emperor took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 壬午，大破直力鞮軍於鐵歧山南，獲其器械輜重，牛羊二十餘萬。

translations.literal: On day renwu, greatly defeated Zhiligidi's army south of Tieqi Mountain, capturing their weapons, baggage, and more than two hundred thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day he shattered Zhiligidi's army south of Tieqi Mountain and seized arms, wagons, and more than two hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 戊子，自五原金津南渡河。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, crossed the river south from Jinyuan Ford at Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day he forded the Yellow River south from Jinyuan at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，次其所居悅跋城，衞辰父子奔遁。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, halted at their residence Yueba City; Weichen father and son fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day he reached their stronghold at Yueba; Weichen and his son fled.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔諸將追之，擒直力鞮。

translations.literal: On day renchen, ordered the generals to pursue and captured Zhiligidi.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day he ordered his generals in pursuit and took Zhiligidi alive.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，獲衞辰尸，斬以徇，遂滅之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: obtained Weichen's corpse, beheaded and displayed it, then destroyed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he recovered Weichen's body, had it beheaded and paraded, and extinguished his line.

sentences.zh: 語在衞辰傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of Weichen.

sentences.zh: 衞辰少子屈丐，亡奔薛干部。

translations.literal: Weichen's youngest son Qu Fu fled to the Xuegan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Weichen's youngest son Qu Fu escaped to the Xuegan tribe.

sentences.zh: [6]車駕次于鹽池。

translations.literal: [6] The imperial carriage halted at Salt Pool.
translations.idiomatic: [6] The court encamped at Salt Pool.

sentences.zh: 自河已南，諸部悉平。

translations.literal: From the river southward, all tribes were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river every tribe was brought to submission.

sentences.zh: 簿其珍寶畜產，名馬三十餘萬匹，牛羊四百餘萬頭。

translations.literal: Registered their treasures and livestock: more than three hundred thousand famous horses, more than four million cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He inventoried their wealth and herds: over three hundred thousand fine horses and more than four million cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 班賜大臣各有差。

translations.literal: Distributed rewards to great ministers each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded his chief ministers according to their stations.

sentences.zh: 收衞辰子弟宗黨無少長五千餘人，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Took Weichen's sons, younger brothers, and clansmen young and old, more than five thousand persons, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: More than five thousand of Weichen's kin, young and old, were seized and put to death.

sentences.zh: 山胡酋大幡頹、業易于等率三千餘家降附，出居于馬邑。

translations.literal: Shanhu chiefs Dafantui, Yeyiyu, and others led more than three thousand households to submit and were settled at Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Dafantui and Yeyiyu of the Shanhu, with more than three thousand households, submitted and were resettled at Mayi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，起河南宮。

translations.literal: That year, built Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year he began the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月，幸木根山，遂次黑鹽池。

translations.literal: Year 7, spring, first month: visited Mugen Mountain, then halted at Black Salt Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, in the first month of spring, he went to Mugen Mountain and then encamped at Black Salt Pool.

sentences.zh: 饗宴羣臣，覲諸國貢使。

translations.literal: Feasted the host of ministers and received tribute envoys from various states.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his ministers and received envoys bearing tribute from the surrounding states.

sentences.zh: 北之美水。

translations.literal: North to Meishui.
translations.idiomatic: He continued north to Meishui.

sentences.zh: 三月甲子，宴羣臣於水濱，還幸河南宮。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiazi: feasted ministers at the waterside, returned and visited Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the third month he banqueted his ministers on the riverbank, then returned to the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 西部泣黎大人茂鮮叛走，遣南部大人長孫嵩追討，大破之。

translations.literal: Western Qili grandee Maoxian rebelled and fled; sent southern grandee Zhangsun Song in pursuit and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxian, chieftain of the western Qili, rose in revolt and fled; Zhangsun Song was sent in pursuit and routed him.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，班賜諸官馬牛羊各有差。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: distributed horses, cattle, and sheep to officials each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he gave horses, cattle, and sheep to his officials according to rank.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，行幸漠南，仍築巡臺。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month: traveled to south of the desert, also built a patrol platform.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he toured south of the desert and built a patrol platform.

sentences.zh: 冬十有二月，慕容永遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month: Murong Yong sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter Murong Yong sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，皇子嗣生。

translations.literal: That year, the imperial son Si was born.
translations.idiomatic: That year the prince Si was born.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月，帝南巡。

translations.literal: Year 8, spring, first month: the emperor made a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, in the first month of spring, the emperor toured the south.

sentences.zh: 二月，幸羖羊原，赴白樓。

translations.literal: Second month: visited Goyang Plain, proceeded to Bailou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he went to Goyang Plain and on to Bailou.

sentences.zh: 三月，車駕西征侯呂隣部。

translations.literal: Third month: the imperial carriage west to campaign against the Houlülin tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court marched west against the Houlülin.

translations.literal: Source annotation [7].
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note [7].

sentences.zh: 夏四月，至苦水，大破之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: reached Kushui, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he reached Kushui and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 五月，還幸白樓。

translations.literal: Fifth month: returned and visited Bailou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he returned to Bailou.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂討慕容永於長子。

translations.literal: Murong Chui attacked Murong Yong at Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui besieged Murong Yong at Changzi.

sentences.zh: 六月，車駕北巡。

translations.literal: Sixth month: the imperial carriage made a northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the court toured the north.

sentences.zh: 永來告急，遣陳留公元虔、將軍庾岳率騎五萬東度河救之。

translations.literal: Yong came reporting urgency; sent Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian and General Yu Yue leading fifty thousand cavalry east across the river to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent word that he was hard pressed; the emperor dispatched Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu and General Yu Yue with fifty thousand horsemen east across the river to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 破類拔部帥劉曜等，徙其部落。

translations.literal: Defeated Leiba division commander Liu Yao and others, relocated their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: They defeated Liu Yao, chief of the Leiba division, and resettled his people.

sentences.zh: 元虔等因屯秀容，慕容垂遂圍長子。

translations.literal: Yuan Qian and others therefore camped at Xiurong; Murong Chui then besieged Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian's force encamped at Xiurong while Murong Chui tightened the siege of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，車駕臨幸新壇。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage visited Xintan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court visited Xintan.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，宴羣臣，仍講武。

translations.literal: On day gengyin, feasted ministers and again conducted martial exercises.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day he feasted his ministers and held another military review.

sentences.zh: 先是，衞辰子屈丐奔薛干部，徵之不送。

translations.literal: Earlier, Weichen's son Qu Fu had fled to the Xuegan tribe; they were summoned to hand him over but did not.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qu Fu, Weichen's son, had taken refuge with the Xuegan; when the court demanded his surrender, they refused.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝南征薛干部帥太悉佛於三城，會其先出擊曹覆，帝乘虛屠其城，獲太悉佛子珍寶，徙其民而還。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the emperor southern campaign against Xuegan chief Taxisifu at Sancheng; as it happened they had gone out earlier to attack Cao Fu; the emperor seized the vacancy and slaughtered their city, captured Taxisifu's sons and treasures, relocated the people and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he marched south against Taxisifu of the Xuegan at Sancheng. Taxisifu had already led his men out against Cao Fu; the emperor struck the empty city, slaughtered it, seized his sons and treasure, resettled the people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太悉佛聞之，來赴不及，遂奔姚興。

translations.literal: Taxisifu heard of it, came but could not arrive in time, then fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Taxisifu hurried back too late and fled to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 九月，還幸河南宮。

translations.literal: Ninth month: returned and visited Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，姚萇死。

translations.literal: That year, Yao Chang died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yao Chang died.

sentences.zh: 九年春三月，帝北巡。

translations.literal: Year 9, spring, third month: the emperor made a northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, in the third month of spring, the emperor toured the north.

sentences.zh: 使東平公元儀屯田於河北五原，至於棝楊塞外。

translations.literal: Sent Dongping Prince Yuan Yi to garrison-farm in Wuyuan north of the river, reaching beyond Puyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He set Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping to farm garrisons in Wuyuan north of the river, as far as beyond Puyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，田於河東。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: farmed at Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he oversaw farming at Hedong.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，還幸河南宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: returned and visited Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he returned to the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，蠕蠕社崙等率部落西走。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Rouran Shelun and others led their tribes west in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Shelun of the Rouran led his tribes west in flight.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set out in the Rouran biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 是歲，姚萇子興僭立，殺苻登。

translations.literal: That year, Yao Chang's son Xing presumptuously established himself and killed Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yao Chang's son Xing declared himself emperor in defiance of the court and killed Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂滅永。

translations.literal: Murong Chui destroyed Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui overthrew Murong Yong.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月，太悉佛自長安還嶺北，上郡以西皆應之。

translations.literal: Year 10, spring, first month: Taxisifu from Chang'an returned to north of the ridges; west of Shang commandery all responded.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, in the first month of spring, Taxisifu returned from Chang'an to the country north of the ridges, and the region west of Shang commandery rose for him.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，幸鹽池。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: visited Salt Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he went to Salt Pool.

sentences.zh: 六月，還幸河南宮。

translations.literal: Sixth month: returned and visited Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he returned to the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，慕容垂遣其子寶來寇五原，造舟收穀。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Murong Chui sent his son Bao to raid Wuyuan, building boats to gather grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Murong Chui sent his son Bao against Wuyuan to build boats and gather grain.

sentences.zh: 帝遣右司馬許謙徵兵於姚興。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Right Marshal Xu Qian to levy troops from Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Right Marshal Xu Qian to raise troops from Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 東平公元儀徙據朔方。

translations.literal: Dongping Prince Yuan Yi moved to hold Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping shifted his base to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝親治兵於河南。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the emperor personally drilled troops at Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor personally reviewed the army at Henan.

sentences.zh: 九月，進師，臨河築臺告津，連旌沿河東西千里有餘。

translations.literal: Ninth month: advanced the army, built a platform by the river to announce the crossing, continuous banners along the river east and west for more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he advanced, raised a platform on the riverbank to proclaim the crossing, and stretched his banners along the Yellow River for more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 是時，陳留公元虔五萬騎在東，以絕其左，元儀五萬騎在河北，以承其後，略陽公元遵七萬騎塞其中山之路。

translations.literal: At that time, Chenliu Prince Yuan Qian with fifty thousand cavalry in the east to cut off their left; Yuan Yi fifty thousand cavalry north of the river to receive them from behind; Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun seventy thousand cavalry blocked the road through Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Qian of Chenliu lay in wait east of them with fifty thousand horse; Yuan Yi with fifty thousand blocked the north bank; Prince Yuan Zun of Lueyang sealed the passes through Zhongshan with seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛未，寶燒船夜遁。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day xinwei: Bao burned the boats and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the tenth month of winter Bao burned his fleet and stole away by night.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，帝進軍濟河。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day jimao: the emperor advanced the army and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day of the eleventh month the emperor crossed the river in force.

sentences.zh: 乙酉夕，至參合陂。

translations.literal: On the evening of day yiyou, reached Canhe Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of the yiyou day he came to Canhe Marsh.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，大破之。

translations.literal: On day bingxu, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu day he won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 語在寶傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 生擒其陳留王紹、魯陽王倭奴、桂林王道成、濟陰公尹國、北地王世子鍾葵、安定王世子羊兒以下文武將吏數千人，器甲輜重、軍資雜財十餘萬計。

translations.literal: Alive captured the Chenliu King Shao, Luyang King Wonu, Guilin Prince Daocheng, Jiyin Duke Yin Guo, Beidi King's heir Zhongkui, Anding King's heir Yang'er and below civil and military officers and generals numbering several thousand persons, armor and baggage, military supplies and miscellaneous goods reckoned at more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He took alive the Chenliu king Shao, the Luyang king Wonu, the Guilin prince Daocheng, the Jiyin duke Yin Guo, the heir of the king of Beidi Zhongkui, the heir of the king of Anding Yang'er, and thousands of civil and military officers, with arms, wagons, and supplies in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 於俘虜之中擢其才識者賈彝、賈閨、晁崇等與參謀議，憲章故實。

translations.literal: From among captives selected those of talent and learning — Jia Yi, Jia Gui, Chao Chong, and others — to join in counsel and planning, statutes and models of ancient practice.
translations.idiomatic: From the prisoners he chose men of talent — Jia Yi, Jia Gui, Chao Chong, and others — to advise him on laws and precedent.

sentences.zh: 班賞大臣將校各有差。

translations.literal: Distributed rewards to great ministers, generals, and officers each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded his ministers and commanders according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，還幸雲中之盛樂。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: returned and visited Shengle in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned to Shengle in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 夏六月癸酉，遣將軍王建等三軍討寶廣寧太守劉亢泥，斬之，徙其部落。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, day guiyou: sent General Wang Jian and three armies to attack Bao's Guangning administrator Liu Kangni, beheaded him, relocated his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the sixth month of summer he sent General Wang Jian with three columns against Liu Kangni, Bao's administrator of Guangning; Kangni was beheaded and his people resettled.

sentences.zh: 寶上谷太守慕容普隣，捐郡奔走。

translations.literal: Bao's Shanggu administrator Murong Pulins abandoned the commandery and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Pulins, Bao's administrator of Shanggu, abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，皇太后賀氏崩。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, the Empress Dowager of the He clan died.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day the Empress Dowager He died.

sentences.zh: 是月，葬獻明太后。

translations.literal: That month, buried the Xianming Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Xianming Empress Dowager was buried.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，左司馬許謙上書勸進尊號，帝始建天子旌旗，出入警蹕，於是改元。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Left Marshal Xu Qian submitted a memorial urging the exalted title; the emperor first established Son of Heaven banners, entry and exit with imperial guard; thereupon changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Xu Qian urged him to take the imperial title; the emperor first raised the imperial standard and traveled under guard, and proclaimed a new reign era.

sentences.zh: 八月庚寅，治兵于東郊。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day gengyin: drilled troops at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the eighth month he reviewed the army at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 己亥，大舉討慕容寶，帝親勒六軍四十餘萬，南出馬邑，踰于句注，旌旗駱驛二千餘里，鼓行而前，民屋皆震。

translations.literal: On day jihai, great campaign against Murong Bao; the emperor personally led the six armies, more than four hundred thousand, south from Mayi, crossing Juzhu Pass, banners and pennants continuous for more than two thousand li, drums beating as they advanced, civilian houses all shaking.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day he launched a great campaign against Murong Bao. At the head of more than four hundred thousand men he marched south from Mayi over Juzhu Pass; his banners filled the road for two thousand li, the drums rolled forward, and houses trembled in his path.

sentences.zh: 別詔將軍封真等三軍，從東道出襲幽州，圍薊。

translations.literal: Separate order to General Feng Zhen and three armies from the eastern route to raid Youzhou, besiege Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered General Feng Zhen with three columns to strike east, invest Youzhou, and besiege Ji.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，次陽曲，乘西山，臨觀晉陽，命諸將引騎圍脅，已而罷還。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day wuwu: halted at Yangqu, ascended Western Mountain, overlooked Jinyang, ordered generals to lead cavalry in surrounding threat, then soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the ninth month he halted at Yangqu, climbed the western hills to look down on Jinyang, sent his generals to wheel cavalry about the city in feint, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 寶并州牧遼西王農大懼，將妻子棄城夜出，東遁，并州平。

translations.literal: Bao's Bingzhou governor Liaoxi King Nong was greatly afraid, took wife and children, abandoned the city by night and fled east; Bingzhou pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong, Bao's governor of Bingzhou and king of Liaoxi, fled the city by night with his family; Bingzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 初建臺省，置百官，封拜公侯、將軍、刺史、太守，尚書郎已下悉用文人。

translations.literal: First established the terrace departments, set all offices, enfeoffed marquises and dukes, generals, regional inspectors, and administrators; Secretariat gentlemen and below all used literary men.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the central secretariat, appointed the full bureaucracy, enfeoffed nobles and generals and named inspectors and administrators, and staffed the Secretariat and lower offices with literati.

sentences.zh: [8]帝初拓中原，留心慰納，諸士大夫詣軍門者，無少長，皆引入賜見，存問周悉，人得自盡，苟有微能，咸蒙叙用。

translations.literal: [8] When the emperor first expanded into the Central Plains, he paid careful attention to comfort and recruitment; for scholar-officials who came to the army gate, whether young or old, all were led in, granted audience, questioned thoroughly with full courtesy, each man could exhaust his ability, and if there was slight talent, all received appointment and use.
translations.idiomatic: [8] As he first opened the Central Plains, the emperor welcomed every scholar who came to his camp, young or old alike, heard them out, and employed any man of even modest talent.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔輔國將軍奚牧略地晉川，獲慕容寶丹陽王買得等於平陶城。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, ordered Assistant State General Xi Mu to seize territory in Jinchuan, capturing Murong Bao's Prince of Danyang Maide and others at Pingtao City.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day he ordered the Assistant State General Xi Mu into Jinchuan and took Murong Bao's Prince of Danyang Maide and others at Pingtao.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙酉，車駕出井陘，使冠軍將軍王建、左軍將軍李栗五萬騎先驅啟行。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day yiyou: the imperial carriage exited Jingxing Pass, sent Champion General Wang Jian and Left Army General Li Li with fifty thousand cavalry as vanguard to open the march.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the tenth month of winter the court passed Jingxing and sent Wang Jian and Li Li ahead with fifty thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 十有一月庚子朔，帝至真定。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day gengzi on the new moon: the emperor reached Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the eleventh month, the gengzi day, he reached Zhending.

sentences.zh: 自常山以東，守宰或捐城奔竄，或稽顙軍門，唯中山、鄴、信都三城不下。

translations.literal: From Changshan eastward, defending officials either abandoned cities and fled, or bowed forehead at the army gate; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu three cities did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: East of Changshan, magistrates either fled or came to surrender; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu still held out.

sentences.zh: 別詔征東大將軍東平公儀五萬騎南攻鄴，冠軍將軍王建、左軍將軍李栗等攻信都，軍之所行，不得傷民桑棗。

translations.literal: Separate order to Eastern Campaign Grand General Dongping Duke Yi with fifty thousand cavalry south to attack Ye; Champion General Wang Jian, Left Army General Li Li, and others attacked Xindu; where the army passed, they must not harm the people's mulberry trees and jujubes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Grand General Yi of Dongping south against Ye with fifty thousand horse, and Wang Jian and Li Li against Xindu, forbidding any harm to mulberry groves along the line of march.

sentences.zh: 戊午，進軍中山；

translations.literal: On day wuwu, advanced army to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day he advanced on Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 己未，引騎圍之。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, led cavalry to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day he invested the city with cavalry.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「朕量寶不能出戰，必當憑城自守，偷延日月，急攻則傷士，久守則費糧，不如先平鄴、信都，然後還取中山，於計為便。

translations.literal: The emperor told the generals: "I reckon Bao cannot come out to battle and is sure to rely on the city to defend himself, stealing extra days and months; urgent attack then injures the soldiers, long defense then wastes grain — better first pacify Ye and Xindu, then return to take Zhongshan; for planning this is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his generals, "Bao will not meet us in the field; he will hide behind the walls and wait us out. A hasty assault wastes men, a long siege wastes grain. Better to take Ye and Xindu first, then return for Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 若移軍遠去，寶必散眾求食民間，如此，則人心離阻，攻之易克。

translations.literal: If we shift the army far away, Bao is sure to disperse his masses to seek food among the people; thus people's hearts will part and resist, and attack will be easy to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If we draw off, he will send his troops to forage among the villages, the people will turn against him, and the city will fall the more easily."

sentences.zh: 」諸將稱善。

translations.literal: The generals all praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: His officers agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，車駕幸魯口城。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, the imperial carriage visited Lukou City.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day the court moved to Lukou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，司馬昌明死，子德宗僭立，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year, Sima Changming died; his son Dezong presumptuously established himself and sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Changming died; his son Dezong seized the throne and sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 呂光僭稱天王，號大涼，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Lü Guang presumptuously styled himself Heavenly King, era name Great Liang, sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang declared himself Heavenly King of Great Liang and also sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月己亥朔，大饗羣臣於魯口。

translations.literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day jihai on the new moon: great feast for the host of ministers at Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the new moon of the first month of spring, the jihai day, he held a great feast for his ministers at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶遣其左衞將軍慕容騰寇博陵，殺中山太守及高陽諸縣令長，抄掠租運。

translations.literal: Murong Bao sent his Left Guard General Murong Teng to raid Boling, killing the Zhongshan administrator and the magistrates of Gaoyang counties, plundering tax grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao sent Murong Teng to strike Boling, kill the Zhongshan administrator and several Gaoyang magistrates, and seize tax grain.

sentences.zh: 是時信都未下，庚申，乃進軍。

translations.literal: At that time Xindu had not yet fallen; on day gengshen, then advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xindu still held out; on the gengshen day he marched against it.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，引騎圍之。

translations.literal: On day renxu, led cavalry to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day he besieged it with cavalry.

sentences.zh: 其夜，寶冀州刺史宜都王慕容鳳踰城奔走，歸于中山。

translations.literal: That night, Bao's Jizhou inspector Prince of Yidu Murong Feng crossed the wall and fled, returning to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: That night Murong Feng, Bao's inspector of Jizhou and prince of Yidu, fled over the wall back to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，寶輔國將軍張驤、護軍將軍徐超率將吏已下舉城降。

translations.literal: On day guihai, Bao's Assistant State General Zhang Nang and Protecting Army General Xu Chao led officers and clerks and below to raise the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day Zhang Nang and Xu Chao, Bao's generals, surrendered the city with all their officers.

sentences.zh: 寶聞帝幸信都，乃趣博陵之深澤，屯呼沱水，遣弟賀麟寇楊城，殺常山守兵三百餘人。

translations.literal: Bao heard the emperor was visiting Xindu, then hurried to Shenze in Boling, encamped at the Hutuo River, sent his younger brother Helin to raid Yangcheng, killing more than three hundred Changshan garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the emperor was at Xindu, Bao rushed to Shenze on the Hutuo, sent his brother Helin against Yangcheng, and killed more than three hundred Changshan defenders.

sentences.zh: 寶悉出珍寶及宮人招募郡縣，羣盜無賴者多應之。

translations.literal: Bao brought out all treasures and palace women to recruit commanderies and counties; many bandits and ruffians responded.
translations.idiomatic: Bao emptied his treasury and sent out palace women to raise levies; ruffians and outlaws flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 二月己巳，帝進幸楊城。

translations.literal: Second month, day jisi: the emperor advanced and visited Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the second month the emperor advanced to Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，軍于鉅鹿之栢肆塢，臨呼沱水。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, army at Baixi Mound in Julu, overlooking the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day he encamped at Baixi Mound in Julu, facing the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 其夜，寶悉眾犯營，燎及行宮，兵人駭散。

translations.literal: That night, Bao led his entire host to attack the camp; fire reached the traveling palace; soldiers and men panicked and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bao attacked with his whole army; fire reached the imperial quarters and the troops broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 帝驚起，不及衣冠，跣出擊鼓。

translations.literal: The emperor startled awake, had no time for cap and clothes, barefoot went out and beat the drum.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaped up barefoot, without cap or robe, and beat the alarm drum.

sentences.zh: 俄而左右及中軍將士，稍稍來集。

translations.literal: Before long attendants left and right and central army officers and soldiers gradually came to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his guards and the central army gathered around him.

sentences.zh: 帝設奇陳，列烽營外，縱騎衝之，寶眾大敗，斬首萬餘級，擒其將軍高長等四千餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor set a stratagem formation, arrayed beacon fires outside the camp, released cavalry to charge them; Bao's masses were greatly defeated, beheaded more than ten thousand, captured their generals Gao Chang and others more than four thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He formed an ambush, lit beacons outside the camp, and charged with cavalry. Bao's army was shattered; more than ten thousand were killed and four thousand taken, including the general Gao Chang.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，寶走中山，獲其器仗輜重數十萬計。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Bao fled to Zhongshan; obtained their weapons, baggage, and stores reckoned at several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day Bao fled to Zhongshan, leaving arms and baggage in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 寶尚書閔亮、秘書監崔逞、太常孫沂、殿中侍御史孟輔等並降。

translations.literal: Bao's Secretariat Director Min Liang, Secretariat Supervisor Cui Huang, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Sun Yi, Palace Attendant Censor Meng Fu, and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Min Liang, Cui Huang, Sun Yi, Meng Fu, and other officers of Bao's court surrendered.

sentences.zh: 降者相屬，賜拜職爵各有差。

translations.literal: Surrenderers followed one after another; bestowed offices and ranks each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Surrenders poured in, and each man was rewarded with office and rank.

sentences.zh: 平原徐超聚眾反於畔城，詔將軍奚辱捕斬之。

translations.literal: Xu Chao of Pingyuan gathered masses in revolt at Pancheng; ordered General Xi Ru to capture and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chao of Pingyuan rose at Pancheng; General Xi Ru was sent to capture and execute him.

sentences.zh: 并州守將封真率其種族與徒何為逆，將攻刺史元延，延討平之。

translations.literal: Bingzhou defending general Feng Zhen led his tribe and together with Tujie made rebellion, intending to attack Regional Inspector Yuan Yan; Yan attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhen of Bingzhou rebelled with his tribe and the Tujie, planning to strike the inspector Yuan Yan, who defeated and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 是時，栢肆之役，遠近流言，賀蘭部帥附力眷、紇突隣部帥匿物尼、紇奚部帥叱奴根聚黨反於陰館，南安公元順率軍討之，不克，死者數千。

translations.literal: At that time, from the battle at Baixi distant and near rumors spread; Helan division chief Fuli Juan, Hetulin division chief Niwuni, Hexi division chief Chinu Gen gathered parties in revolt at Yinyang; Prince of Nan'an Yuan Shun led army to attack them, could not overcome, dead numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Baixi, tribes rose in the north: Fuli Juan of the Helan, Niwuni of the Hetulin, and Chinu Gen of the Hexi rebelled at Yinyang. Prince Yuan Shun of Nan'an attacked them but failed, losing thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 詔安遠將軍庾岳總萬騎，還討叱奴根等，滅之。

translations.literal: Ordered Pacifying the Distance General Yu Yue to command ten thousand cavalry, return to attack Chinu Gen and others, and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue was ordered back with ten thousand horse; he destroyed Chinu Gen and his allies.

sentences.zh: 三月己酉，車駕次于盧奴。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiyou: the imperial carriage halted at Lunu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the third month the court halted at Lunu.

sentences.zh: 寶遣使求和，請送元觚，割常山以西奉國，乞守中山以東，帝許之。

translations.literal: Bao sent envoys seeking peace, requesting to send Yuan Gu, cede west of Changshan to serve the state, beg to hold east of Zhongshan; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sued for peace, offering to return Yuan Gu, cede everything west of Changshan, and keep only the country east of Zhongshan; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 已而寶背約。

translations.literal: Before long Bao broke the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Bao soon broke the truce.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，車駕次中山，命諸將圍之。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, the imperial carriage halted at Zhongshan, ordered the generals to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day he invested Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 是夜，寶弟賀麟將妻子出走西山。

translations.literal: That night, Bao's younger brother Helin led wife and children and fled to Western Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bao's brother Helin fled west into the hills with his family.

sentences.zh: 寶見賀麟走，恐先據和龍，壬子夜，遂將其妻子及兄弟宗族數千騎北遁。

translations.literal: Bao saw Helin flee, feared he would first seize Helong; on the night of day renzi, then led his wife and children and brothers and clansmen several thousand cavalry north in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Helin would seize Helong first, Bao fled north on the renzi night with his family and several thousand kin.

sentences.zh: 寶將李沈、王次多、張超、賈歸等來降。

translations.literal: Bao's generals Li Shen, Wang Ciduo, Zhang Chao, Jia Gui, and others came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, Wang Ciduo, Zhang Chao, Jia Gui, and other of Bao's generals submitted.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍長孫肥追之，至范陽，不及而還。

translations.literal: Sent General Zhangsun Fei in pursuit; reached Fanyang, could not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Fei pursued as far as Fanyang but could not overtake him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 城內共立慕容普隣為主。

translations.literal: Within the city together established Murong Pulins as lord.
translations.idiomatic: The city set up Murong Pulins as its ruler.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，帝以軍糧未繼，乃詔征東大將軍東平公元儀罷鄴圍，徙屯鉅鹿，積租楊城。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: the emperor because army grain had not yet arrived, then ordered Eastern Campaign Grand General Dongping Prince Yuan Yi to lift the siege of Ye, move camp to Julu, accumulate rent at Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, with supplies still short, he ordered Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping to raise the siege of Ye, move to Julu, and gather grain at Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 普隣出步卒六千餘人，伺間犯諸屯兵，詔將軍長孫肥等輕騎挑之，帝以虎隊五千橫截其後，斬首五千，生虜七百人，宥而遣之。

translations.literal: Pulins sent out infantry more than six thousand men, watching for openings to attack various encampments; ordered General Zhangsun Fei and others with light cavalry to provoke them; the emperor with Tiger Corps five thousand cut off their rear, beheaded five thousand, captured alive seven hundred, pardoned and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Pulins sent out more than six thousand foot to harass the camps. Zhangsun Fei provoked them with light horse; the emperor's Tiger Guard of five thousand cut off their retreat, killed five thousand, took seven hundred alive, and let them go.

sentences.zh: 夏五月庚子，大賞功臣。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day gengzi: great reward for meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the fifth month of summer he rewarded his great ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝以中山城內為普隣所脅，而大軍迫之，欲降無路，及密招喻之。

translations.literal: The emperor because within Zhongshan city they were coerced by Pulins, while the great army pressed them, wishing to surrender but with no road, therefore secretly sent summons and persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the people of Zhongshan were held hostage by Pulins yet longed to yield, he sent secret appeals to them.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，曜兵揚威以示城內，命諸軍罷圍南徙以待其變。

translations.literal: On day jiachen, displayed troops to show might to those within the city, ordered all armies to lift siege and move south to await their change.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day he paraded his host before the walls, then drew the armies south to wait for the city to turn.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以東平公元儀為驃騎大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、兗豫雍荊徐揚六州牧、左丞相，封衞王。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, appointed Dongping Prince Yuan Yi as Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Governor of the Six Provinces Yan, Yu, Yong, Jing, Xu, and Yang, Left Chancellor, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day he made Prince Yuan Yi of Dongping Grand General of Agile Cavalry, supreme commander, governor of six provinces, left chancellor, and prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 襄城公元題，進封為王。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangcheng Yuan Ti advanced enfeoffment to prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ti of Xiangcheng was raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，普隣遣烏丸張驤率五千餘人出城求食，寇常山之靈壽，殺害吏民。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Pulins sent Wuhuan Zhang Nang leading more than five thousand men out of the city to seek food, raiding Lingshou in Changshan, killing officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Pulins sent the Wuhuan Zhang Nang with more than five thousand men out to forage; they ravaged Lingshou in Changshan and killed officials and civilians.

sentences.zh: 賀麟自丁零中入于驤軍，因其眾，復入中山，殺普隣而自立。

translations.literal: Helin from among the Dingling entered Zhang Nang's army; relying on his masses, again entered Zhongshan, killed Pulins and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: Helin joined Zhang Nang from the Dingling tribes, re-entered Zhongshan, killed Pulins, and declared himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 帝還幸魯口，遣將軍長孫肥一千騎襲中山，入其郛而還。

translations.literal: The emperor returned and visited Lukou, sent General Zhangsun Fei with one thousand cavalry to raid Zhongshan, entered the outer wall and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to Lukou and sent Zhangsun Fei with a thousand horse to strike Zhongshan, enter the outer wall, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 八月丙寅朔，帝自魯口進軍常山之九門。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day bingyin on the new moon: the emperor from Lukou advanced army to Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the eighth month, the bingyin day, he marched from Lukou to Jiumen in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 時大疫，人馬牛多死。

translations.literal: At that time great pestilence; men, horses, and cattle mostly died.
translations.idiomatic: A great pestilence swept the army; men, horses, and cattle died in masses.

sentences.zh: 帝問疫於諸將，對曰：「在者纔十四五。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the generals about the pestilence; they replied: "Of those who remain, barely fourteen or fifteen in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He asked his officers how many still stood fit for duty; they said barely one man in seven remained.

sentences.zh: 」是時中山猶拒守，而饑疫並臻，羣下咸思還北。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongshan still resisted defense, while famine and pestilence both arrived; the host below all thought of returning north.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan still held out, famine and plague together afflicted the host, and every officer wished to march north.

sentences.zh: 帝知其意，因謂之曰：「斯固天命，將若之何！

translations.literal: The emperor knew their intent, therefore told them: "This is indeed Heaven's mandate — what can be done about it!
translations.idiomatic: Reading their minds, he said, "This is Heaven's will — what is there to do?

sentences.zh: 四海之人，皆可與為國，在吾所以撫之耳，何恤乎無民！

translations.literal: All men under the four seas can together become the state; in my manner of comforting them lies the answer — why worry about having no people!
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven may be made into a realm; it is for me to win them — why fear an empty land!"

sentences.zh: 」羣臣乃不敢復言。

translations.literal: The host of ministers then did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak of retreat again.

sentences.zh: 遣撫軍大將軍略陽公元遵襲中山，芟其禾䒩，入郛而還。

translations.literal: Sent Pacifying the Army Grand General Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun to raid Zhongshan, mowed their grain and fodder, entered the outer wall and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Yuan Zun of Lueyang to cut Zhongshan's crops, enter the outer wall, and return.

sentences.zh: 九月，賀麟飢窮，率三萬餘人出寇新巿。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Helin hungry and destitute, led more than thirty thousand men out to raid Xinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Helin, starving, led more than thirty thousand men against Xinshi.

sentences.zh: 甲子晦，帝進軍討之，太史令晁崇奏曰：「不吉。

translations.literal: On day jiazi at month's end, the emperor advanced army to attack them; Grand Astrologer Chao Chong memorialized saying: "Not auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month, the jiazi day, he marched to meet them; the Grand Astrologer Chao Chong warned that the day was ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「其義云何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What is the meaning?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what he meant.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔紂以甲子亡，兵家忌之。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Formerly Zhou of Shang perished on jiazi; military families taboo it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "King Zhou of Shang fell on a jiazi day; soldiers have long feared that date."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「紂以甲子亡，周武不以甲子勝乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Zhou of Shang perished on jiazi — did King Wu of Zhou not win on jiazi?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhou fell on jiazi — did King Wu of Zhou not win on jiazi?"

sentences.zh: 」崇無以對。

translations.literal: " Chong had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙寅，帝進軍新巿，賀麟退阻泒水，依漸洳澤以自固。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingyin: the emperor advanced army to Xinshi; Helin retreated to block the Fushui, relied on the Jianru marshes to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the tenth month of winter he advanced on Xinshi. Helin fell back to the Fushui and entrenched in the Jianru marshes.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝臨其營，戰於義臺塢，大破之，斬首九千餘級。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, the emperor approached their camp, battled at Yitai Mound, greatly defeated them, beheaded more than nine thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he assaulted their camp at Yitai Mound, killed more than nine thousand, and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 賀麟單馬走西山，遂奔鄴，慕容德殺之。

translations.literal: Helin alone on horse fled to Western Mountain, then fled to Ye; Murong De killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Helin fled alone into the western hills, then to Ye, where Murong De killed him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，其所署公卿、尚書、將吏、士卒降者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, those he had appointed as dukes and ministers, Secretariat, generals, officers, and soldiers who surrendered numbered more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day more than twenty thousand of his appointed officials, generals, and soldiers surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其將張驤、李沈、慕容文等先來降，尋皆亡還，是日復獲之，皆赦而不問。

translations.literal: His generals Zhang Nang, Li Shen, Murong Wen, and others had earlier come to surrender, soon all fled back; that day captured them again, all pardoned and not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Nang, Li Shen, Murong Wen, and others who had surrendered and fled were taken again that day and pardoned without punishment.

sentences.zh: 獲其所傳皇帝璽綬、圖書、府庫、珍寶，簿列數萬。

translations.literal: Obtained the imperial seal and cord, documents, treasuries, and precious things they transmitted, registered in lists of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the imperial seal and cord, the archives, the treasury, and treasure beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 班賜功臣及將士各有差。

translations.literal: Distributed rewards to meritorious ministers and officers and soldiers each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded ministers and soldiers according to merit.

sentences.zh: 中山平。

translations.literal: Zhongshan pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，襄城王題薨。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, Prince of Xiangcheng Ti died.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day Prince Yuan Ti of Xiangcheng died.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，遣三萬騎赴衞王儀，將以攻鄴。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, sent thirty thousand cavalry to join Prince of Wei Yi, intending to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day he sent thirty thousand horse to Prince Yi of Wei for the assault on Ye.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鮮卑禿髮烏孤私署大單于、西平王。

translations.literal: That year, Xianbei Tufa Wugu privately styled himself Great Chanyu, Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Xianbei leader Tufa Wugu took the titles Great Chanyu and Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 天興元年春正月，慕容德走保滑臺，儀克鄴，收其倉庫。

translations.literal: Tianxing year 1, spring, first month: Murong De fled to hold Huatai; Yi captured Ye and collected its granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing, in the first month of spring, Murong De withdrew to Huatai; Yi took Ye and its granaries.

sentences.zh: 詔賞將士各有差。

translations.literal: Ordered reward for officers and soldiers each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered rewards for the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 儀追德至於河，不及而還。

translations.literal: Yi pursued De to the river, could not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yi pursued De to the river but could not overtake him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 庚子，車駕自中山行幸常山之真定，次趙郡之高邑，遂幸于鄴。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, the imperial carriage from Zhongshan traveled to Zhending in Changshan, halted at Gaoyi in Zhao commandery, then visited Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day the court went from Zhongshan to Zhending in Changshan, halted at Gaoyi in Zhao, and then entered Ye.
