sentences.zh: 民有老不能自存者，詔郡縣賑恤之。

translations.literal: For people who were old and could not support themselves, ordered commanderies and counties to relieve and succor them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the commanderies to succor the aged who could not support themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝至鄴，巡登臺榭，遍覽宮城，將有定都之意。

translations.literal: The emperor reached Ye, toured ascending terraces and towers, viewed throughout the palace city, intending to fix the capital there.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye he climbed the terraces, surveyed the palace, and considered making it his capital.

sentences.zh: 乃置行臺，以龍驤將軍日南公和跋為尚書，與左丞賈彝率郎吏及兵五千人鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Thereupon established a traveling secretariat; appointed Dragon Cavalry General Prince of Rinan He Ba as Secretariat Director, with Left Assistant Jia Yi leading clerks and soldiers five thousand men to garrison Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a traveling secretariat, named Prince He Ba of Rinan director, and left Jia Yi with five thousand clerks and troops to hold Ye.

sentences.zh: 車駕自鄴還中山，所過存問百姓。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage from Ye returned to Zhongshan; where it passed, inquired after and comforted the people.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Ye to Zhongshan, he inquired after the people along the route.

sentences.zh: 詔大軍所經州郡，復貲租一年，除山東民租賦之半。

translations.literal: Ordered the commanderies and prefectures the great army passed through to remit tax one year, exempted half the rent and levies of the people east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted one year's taxes in every district the army had crossed and halved the levies east of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 東駕將北還，發卒萬人治直道，自望都鐵關鑿恒嶺至代五百餘里。

translations.literal: The eastern journey about to return north, mobilized ten thousand men to repair the straight road, from Wangdu Iron Pass chiseled through Heng Ridge to Dai more than five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Preparing to march north, he set ten thousand men to cut a straight road from Wangdu through Heng Ridge to Dai, more than five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 帝慮還後山東有變，乃置行臺於中山，詔左丞相、守尚書令、衞王儀鎮中山，撫軍大將軍、略陽公元遵鎮勃海之合口。

translations.literal: The emperor feared after returning that east of the mountains there would be trouble, therefore established a traveling secretariat at Zhongshan, ordered Left Chancellor, Guardian Secretariat Director, Prince of Wei Yi to garrison Zhongshan, Pacifying the Army Grand General Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun to garrison He Pass in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing trouble in the east after his departure, he left a traveling secretariat at Zhongshan under Prince Yi of Wei and stationed Prince Yuan Zun of Lueyang at He Pass in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍尹國先督租于冀州，聞帝將還，謀反，欲襲信都，安南將軍長孫嵩執送，斬之。

translations.literal: Right Army General Yin Guo earlier supervised rent in Jizhou; hearing the emperor would return, plotted rebellion, intended to raid Xindu; Pacifying the South General Zhangsun Song arrested and sent him, beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guo, who had been collecting rent in Jizhou, plotted rebellion when he heard the emperor was leaving; Zhangsun Song seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，車駕發自中山，至于望都堯山。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, the imperial carriage set out from Zhongshan, reaching Yaoshan in Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day the court left Zhongshan for Yaoshan in Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 徙山東六州民吏及徒何、高麗雜夷三十六萬，百工伎巧十萬餘口，以充京師。

translations.literal: Relocated the people, officials, and clerks of the six provinces east of the mountains and Tujie, Gaoli, and various Yi thirty-six myriads, artisans and craftsmen more than one hundred thousand mouths, to fill the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He moved three hundred and sixty thousand families from the six eastern provinces, together with Tujie, Koguryo, and other tribes, and more than a hundred thousand artisans, to fill the capital.

sentences.zh: [9]車駕次于恒山之陽。

translations.literal: [9] The imperial carriage halted at the south of Heng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: [9] The court halted south of Heng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 博陵、勃海、章武羣盜並起，略陽公元遵等討平之。

translations.literal: Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu bandits all rose; Lueyang Prince Yuan Zun and others attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu; Yuan Zun and others suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 廣川太守賀盧殺冀州刺史王輔，驅勒守兵，抄掠陽平、頓丘諸郡，遂南渡河，奔慕容德。

translations.literal: Guangchuan Administrator He Lu killed Jizhou Regional Inspector Wang Fu, drove and compelled garrison troops, plundered Yangping and Dunqiu commanderies, then south crossed the river, fled to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: He Lu, administrator of Guangchuan, killed the inspector Wang Fu, pressed the garrisons into revolt, raided Yangping and Dunqiu, crossed the river south, and fled to Murong De.

sentences.zh: 二月，車駕自中山幸繁畤宮，更選屯衞。

translations.literal: Second month: the imperial carriage from Zhongshan visited Fanchi Palace, again selected garrison guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the court went from Zhongshan to Fanchi Palace and reorganized the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 詔給內徙新民耕牛，計口受田。

translations.literal: Ordered giving newly settled inner migrants plow oxen, calculating mouths to receive fields.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered plow oxen given to the newly resettled colonists and land allotted by household.

sentences.zh: 三月，離石胡帥呼延鐵、西河胡帥張崇等聚黨數千人叛，詔安遠將軍庾岳討平之。

translations.literal: Third month: Lishi Hu chief Huyan Tie, Xihe Hu chief Zhang Chong, and others gathered parties of several thousand in rebellion; ordered Pacifying the Distance General Yu Yue to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Huyan Tie of Lishi and Zhang Chong of Xihe rebelled with thousands of followers; Yu Yue was sent to crush them.

sentences.zh: 漁陽羣盜庫傉官韜聚眾反。

translations.literal: Yuyang bandit Kuluguan Tao gathered masses in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Kuluguan Tao of Yuyang raised a bandit host.

sentences.zh: 詔中堅將軍伊謂討之。

translations.literal: Ordered Central Firm General Yi Wei to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Central Firm General Yi Wei to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 徵左丞相、衞王儀還京師，詔略陽公遵代鎮中山。

translations.literal: Summoned Left Chancellor, Prince of Wei Yi back to the capital; ordered Lueyang Duke Zun to replace him garrisoning Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Wei was recalled to the capital, and Duke Zun of Lueyang was left to hold Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬戌，進遵封常山王，南安公元順進封毗陵王，征虜將軍歷陽公穆崇為太尉，安南將軍鉅鹿公長孫嵩為司徒。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day renxu: advanced Zun's enfeoffment to Prince of Changshan, Prince of Nan'an Yuan Shun advanced enfeoffment to Prince of Piling, Pacifying the Barbarians General Liyang Duke Mu Chong made Grand Marshal, Pacifying the South Duke Zhangsun Song made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the fourth month of summer Zun was made prince of Changshan, Shun prince of Piling, Mu Chong grand marshal, and Zhangsun Song minister of works.

sentences.zh: 帝祠天於西郊，麾幟有加焉。

translations.literal: The emperor sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb; banners and pennants had additions.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb with banners raised in greater splendor.

sentences.zh: 廣平太守、遼西公元意烈謀反，於郡賜死，原其妻子。

translations.literal: Guangping Administrator, Liaoxi Prince Yuan Yilie plotted rebellion; within the commandery granted death, pardoned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yilie of Liaoxi, administrator of Guangping, plotted treason and was ordered to take his own life in the commandery; his wife and children were spared.

sentences.zh: 鄜城屠各董羌、杏城盧水郝奴、河東蜀薛榆、氐帥符興，各率其種內附。

translations.literal: Fucheng Tujue Dong Qiang, Xingcheng Lushui Hao Nu, Hedong Shu Xue Yu, Di chief Fu Xing, each led their tribes to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Qiang of Fucheng, Hao Nu of Xingcheng, Xue Yu of the Shu in Hedong, and the Di chief Fu Xing each brought their tribes in submission.

sentences.zh: 六月丙子，詔有司議定國號。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day bingzi: ordered the relevant offices to discuss and fix the state name.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the sixth month he ordered the ministries to choose a dynastic name.

sentences.zh: 羣臣曰：「昔周秦以前，世居所生之土，有國有家，及王天下，即承為號。

translations.literal: The host of ministers said: "Formerly before Zhou and Qin, generations dwelt in the soil where they were born; having state and family, when they ruled all under Heaven they inherited it as title.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said, "Before Zhou and Qin, rulers took their title from the land where they were born. When they came to rule the world, they kept that name."

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，罷侯置守，時無世繼，其應運而起者，皆不由尺土之資。

translations.literal: From Han onward, marquisates were abolished and defenders appointed; at the time there was no succession by generations; those who rose with the mandate all did not rely on resources of a foot of soil.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han, hereditary fiefs gave way to appointed governors, and men who seized the mandate did not owe their rise to ancestral estates alone.

sentences.zh: 今國家萬世相承，啟基雲代。

translations.literal: Now the state is inherited for ten thousand generations, founding the enterprise at Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Our house is to endure for ten thousand generations, with its foundation in the land of Yun.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為若取長遠，應以代為號。

translations.literal: Your subjects consider that if one takes the long view, one should use Dai as the title.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore urge that, for the long term, the dynasty be called Dai."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「昔朕遠祖，總御幽都，控制遐國，雖踐王位，未定九州。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Formerly my remote ancestor overall governed Youdu, controlled distant states; though he trod the royal throne, he did not fix the Nine Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Long ago our remote ancestor ruled Youdu and held sway over distant realms. Though he bore the royal title, he had not yet united the Nine Provinces.

sentences.zh: 逮于朕躬，處百代之季，天下分裂，諸華乏主。

translations.literal: Reaching my person, residing in the season of the hundredth generation, all under Heaven split apart, the various Hu lacked a lord.
translations.idiomatic: In my own time, at the end of an age of division, the Chinese lands had no true lord.

sentences.zh: [10]民俗雖殊，撫之在德，故躬率六軍，掃平中土，凶逆蕩除，遐邇率服。

translations.literal: [10] Though customs differ, comforting them lies in virtue; therefore I personally lead the six armies, sweep pacify the central land, ferocious rebels are swept away, the distant and near all submit.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Customs may differ, but they are won by virtue. I have therefore led the six armies myself, swept the central plains clean of rebels, and brought the far and near to submission.

sentences.zh: 宜仍先號，以為魏焉。

translations.literal: It is fitting to continue the former title, taking Wei as the name.
translations.idiomatic: It is right to keep our former name and call the state Wei.

sentences.zh: 布告天下，咸知朕意。」

translations.literal: Proclaim throughout all under Heaven, all may know my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed to all under heaven."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，遷都平城，始營宮室，建宗廟，立社稷。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: moved the capital to Pingcheng, first built palace halls, established ancestral temple, set up altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he moved the capital to Pingcheng, began the palace, founded the ancestral temple, and set up the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 漁陽烏丸庫傉官韜復聚黨為寇。

translations.literal: Yuyang Wuhuan Kuluguan Tao again gathered parties as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Kuluguan Tao of the Yuyang Wuhuan rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 詔冠軍將軍王建討平之。

translations.literal: Ordered Champion General Wang Jian to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was sent to crush him.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔有司正封畿，制郊甸，端徑術，標道里，平五權，較五量，定五度。

translations.literal: Eighth month: ordered the relevant offices to correct the capital demesne, regulate suburban fields, straighten roads and measures, mark roads and distances, balance the five weights, compare the five measures, fix the five gradations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he ordered the ministries to survey the capital domain, regulate the suburbs, standardize roads and measures, and fix weights, volumes, and units.

sentences.zh: 遣使循行郡國，舉奏守宰不法者，親覽察黜陟之。

translations.literal: Sent envoys to tour commanderies and kingdoms, memorialize and report unlawful defending officials; personally viewed and inspected dismissals and promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent through the commanderies to report corrupt magistrates, and he personally reviewed their promotions and dismissals.

sentences.zh: 九月，烏丸張驤子超，收合亡命，聚黨三千餘家，據勃海之南皮，自號征東大將軍、烏丸王，抄掠諸郡。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Wuhuan Zhang Nang's son Chao gathered fugitives, assembled parties of more than three thousand households, held Nanpi in Bohai, styled himself Eastern Campaign Grand General, King of the Wuhuan, plundered various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhang Chao, son of the Wuhuan Zhang Nang, gathered three thousand rebel households at Nanpi in Bohai, styled himself king of the Wuhuan and eastern campaign general, and raided the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 詔將軍庾岳討之。

translations.literal: Ordered General Yu Yue to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue was ordered against him.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，起天文殿。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: began the Astronomy Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter work began on the Astronomy Hall.

sentences.zh: 十有一月辛亥，詔尚書吏部郎中鄧淵典官制，立爵品，定律呂，協音樂；

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day xinhai: ordered Secretariat Personnel Section Director Deng Yuan to oversee office regulations, establish noble ranks, fix pitch pipes, harmonize music.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month he put Deng Yuan in charge of offices, ranks, pitch pipes, and music.

sentences.zh: 儀曹郎中董謐撰郊廟、社稷、朝覲、饗宴之儀；

translations.literal: Rituals Section Director Dong Mi compiled rites for suburban altars, altars of soil and grain, court audiences, and feast ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Mi of the rituals section drafted the rites of the suburban sacrifices, the altars, court audiences, and banquets.

sentences.zh: 三公郎中王德定律令，申科禁；

translations.literal: Three Excellencies Section Director Wang De fixed laws and orders, declared prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De of the three excellencies section codified laws and penalties.

sentences.zh: 太史令晁崇造渾儀，考天象；

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Chao Chong made the armillary sphere, examined heavenly signs.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Chong the grand astrologer built an armillary sphere and studied the heavens.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書崔玄伯總而裁之。

translations.literal: Personnel Director Cui Xuanbo overall trimmed and judged them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanbo of the personnel directorate supervised them all.

sentences.zh: 閏月，左丞相、驃騎大將軍、衞王儀及諸王公卿士，詣闕上書曰：「臣等聞宸極居中，則列宿齊其晷；

translations.literal: Intercalary month: Left Chancellor, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Wei Yi and the host of kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars came to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: "Your subjects have heard the pole star at center, then the constellations align their shadows.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Prince Yi of Wei and the nobles and ministers came to court with a memorial: "When the pole stands at the center, the stars wheel in their courses.

sentences.zh: 帝王順天，則羣后仰其度。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven follows Heaven, then the host below look up to his measure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven follows Heaven, all below look up to his measure.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德協二儀，道隆三五，仁風被於四海，盛化塞于大區，澤及昆蟲，恩霑行葦，謳歌所屬，八表歸心，軍威所及，如風靡草，萬姓顒顒，咸思係命。

translations.literal: We bow before Your Majesty's virtue harmonizing the two standards, Way towering to the Three and Five, benevolent wind spread over the four seas, flourishing transformation filling the great region, favor reaching insects, grace soaking trailing reeds, what songs belong to, the eight directions return in heart, where military might reaches, like wind over grass, the myriad people gazing eagerly, all wish to bind their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue matches heaven and earth, your Way rivals the sage kings of old, your grace reaches even the insects and the grass at the roadside, and the eight directions turn to you as the grasses bend before the wind. All the people long to place their lives in your hands.

sentences.zh: 而躬履謙虛，退身後己，宸儀未彰，袞服未御，非所以上允皇天之意，下副樂推之心。

translations.literal: Yet you personally practice humility, withdraw and place yourself after others; imperial bearing not yet displayed, dragon robes not yet worn — this is not what above fulfills Heaven's intent, below matches the heart of those who joyfully push you forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still hold back, refusing the imperial regalia. This neither fulfills Heaven's intent nor the people's wish to raise you up.

sentences.zh: 宜光崇聖烈，示軌憲於萬世。

translations.literal: It is fitting to glorify the sacred enterprise, display models and statutes to ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: You should glorify the sacred enterprise and show the model to ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹昧死以聞。

translations.literal: Your subjects respectfully risk death to report.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you, at the risk of our lives, to accept."

sentences.zh: 」帝三讓乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor thrice declined and then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined three times, then consented.

sentences.zh: 十有二月己丑，帝臨天文殿，太尉、司徒進璽綬，百官咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jichou: the emperor attended the Astronomy Hall; Grand Marshal and Minister of Works advanced the seal and cord; the hundred offices all called ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the twelfth month he took his seat in the Astronomy Hall; the grand marshal and minister of works presented the seal and cord, and the court shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改年。

translations.literal: Great amnesty, changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 追尊成帝已下及后號諡。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored Emperor Cheng and below and empresses with temple names and posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored Emperor Cheng and his predecessors, and gave posthumous titles to the empresses.

sentences.zh: 樂用皇始之舞。

translations.literal: Music used the Huangshi dance.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted the Huangshi dance for state ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 詔百司議定行次，尚書崔玄伯等奏從土德，服色尚黃，數用五，未祖辰臘，犧牲用白，五郊立氣，宣贊時令，敬授民時，行夏之正。

translations.literal: Ordered the hundred offices to discuss and fix the dynastic phase; Secretariat Cui Xuanbo and others memorialized following the Earth phase, dress color esteemed yellow, numbers used five, end-of-year sacrifice at chen, victims used white, five suburbs established qi, proclaimed and assisted the seasons, respectfully bestowed the people's seasons, practiced Xia's correct calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ministries to fix the dynastic element; Cui Xuanbo urged the earth phase, yellow vestments, the number five, white victims, and the Xia calendar.

sentences.zh: 徙六州二十二郡守宰、豪傑、吏民二千家于代都。

translations.literal: Relocated the defending officials, powerful families, and people of two thousand households from six provinces and twenty-two commanderies to the capital at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand leading families from six provinces and twenty-two commanderies were moved to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蘭汗殺慕容寶而自立，寶子盛殺汗僭立。

translations.literal: That year, Lan Han killed Murong Bao and established himself; Bao's son Sheng killed Han and presumptuously established himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lan Han murdered Murong Bao and seized the throne; Bao's son Sheng killed Lan Han and declared himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 慕容德自稱燕王。

translations.literal: Murong De styled himself King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De declared himself King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月甲子，初祠上帝于南郊，以始祖神元皇帝配，降壇視燎，成禮而反。

translations.literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day jiazi: first sacrificed to the Supreme Lord at the southern suburb, with Founding Ancestor Divine Yuan Emperor as associate; descended the altar to view the burning, completed the rites and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the jiazi day of the first month of spring, he first sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb with the Divine Yuan Emperor as associate, watched the burning of the offerings, and returned when the rite was done.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，曲赦京師。

translations.literal: On day yichou, partial amnesty within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day he granted a partial amnesty in the capital.

sentences.zh: 始制三駕之法。

translations.literal: First established the law of three carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted the protocol of the three imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 庚午，車駕北巡，分命諸將大襲高車，大將軍、常山王遵等三軍從東道出長川，鎮北將軍高涼王樂真等七軍從西道出牛川，車駕親勒六軍從中道自駮髯水西北。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, the imperial carriage northern tour, separately ordered the generals in great raids on the Gaoche; Grand General, Prince of Changshan Zun and three armies from the eastern route exited Changchuan, Pacifying the North General Gaoliang Prince Yue Zhen and seven armies from the western route exited Niuchuan, the emperor personally led the six armies from the central route from Bochan Water northwest.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day he toured the north and sent his generals against the Gaoche. Prince Zun of Changshan marched east from Changchuan, Prince Yue Zhen of Gaoliang west from Niuchuan, and the emperor led the central column northwest from Bochan Water.

sentences.zh: 二月丁亥朔，諸軍同會，破高車雜種三十餘部，獲七萬餘口，馬三十餘萬匹，牛羊百四十餘萬。

translations.literal: Second month, day dinghai on the new moon: all armies met together, defeated more than thirty Gaoche mixed tribes, obtained more than seventy thousand persons, more than three hundred thousand horses, more than 1.4 million cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the second month, the dinghai day, the columns united and broke more than thirty Gaoche tribes, taking seventy thousand people, three hundred thousand horses, and 1.4 million head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍、衞王儀督三萬騎別從西北絕漠千餘里，破其遺迸七部，獲二萬餘口，馬五萬餘匹，牛羊二十餘萬頭，高車二十餘萬乘，并服玩諸物。

translations.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Wei Yi commanded thirty thousand cavalry separately from the northwest crossing the desert more than a thousand li, defeated their scattered remnants of seven divisions, obtained more than twenty thousand persons, more than fifty thousand horses, more than two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, Gaoche more than two hundred thousand carts, together with clothing, curios, and various objects.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Wei with thirty thousand horse crossed the desert northwest more than a thousand li, shattered seven remnant bands, and took twenty thousand people, fifty thousand horses, two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, two hundred thousand Gaoche wagons, and countless goods.

sentences.zh: 還次牛川及薄山，並刻石記功，班賜從臣各有差。

translations.literal: Returned and halted at Niuchuan and Bo Mountain, both carved stone to record merit, distributed rewards to accompanying ministers each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The armies halted at Niuchuan and Bo Mountain, carved stones to record their deeds, and rewarded the officers by rank.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，征虜將軍庾岳破張超於勃海。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, Pacifying the Barbarians General Yu Yue defeated Zhang Chao at Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day Yu Yue defeated Zhang Chao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 超走平原，為其黨所殺。

translations.literal: Chao fled to Pingyuan, was killed by his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Chao fled to Pingyuan and was killed by his own followers.

sentences.zh: 以所獲高車眾起鹿苑，南因臺陰，北距長城，東包白登，屬之西山，廣輪數十里，鑿渠引武川水注之苑中，疏為三溝，分流宮城內外。

translations.literal: Using the captured Gaoche masses, raised a deer park; south leaning on the terrace shade, north reaching the Long Wall, east enclosing Baideng, attached to Western Mountain, circumference several tens of li, chiseled canals to lead Wuchuan water into the park, dredged into three channels, divided flow inside and outside the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: With the Gaoche captives he built a deer park south of the terrace, north to the Long Wall, east to Baideng, and west to the western hills, several tens of li around, and dug canals from the Wuchuan to feed three channels through and around the palace.

sentences.zh: 又穿鴻雁池。

translations.literal: Also dug Wild Goose Pool.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug the Wild Goose Pool.

sentences.zh: 三月己未，車駕至自北伐。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiwei: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the third month the court returned from the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 甲子，初令五經羣書各置博士，增國子太學生員三千人。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, first ordered the Five Classics and collected books each to set a Erudite, increased National University students by three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day he appointed erudites for the Five Classics, enlarged the National University by three thousand students.

sentences.zh: 是月，氐人李辯叛慕容德，求援於鄴行臺尚書和跋，跋輕騎往應之，克滑臺，收德宮人府藏；

translations.literal: That month, Di man Li Bian rebelled against Murong De, sought rescue from Ye traveling Secretariat Director He Ba; Ba with light cavalry went to respond, captured Huatai, collected De's palace women and treasury.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Di leader Li Bian rebelled against Murong De and called on He Ba at Ye; Ba rode to Huatai, took the city, and seized De's palace women and treasury.

sentences.zh: 又破德桂林王鎮及郎吏將士千餘人。

translations.literal: Also defeated De's Guilin King garrison and clerks, generals, and soldiers more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the garrison of De's Guilin king and more than a thousand officers and men.

sentences.zh: 丙子，遣建義將軍庾真、越騎校尉奚斤討厙狄部帥葉亦干、宥連部帥竇羽泥於太渾川，破之，厙狄懃支子沓亦干率其部落內附。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, sent Establishing Righteousness General Yu Zhen, Rapid-as-Horses Commandant Xi Jin to attack Kudi division chief Ye Yigan, Youlian division chief Dou Yuni at Taihun River, defeated them; Kudi Qinzhi's son Tayeigan led his tribe to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day he sent Yu Zhen and Xi Jin against Ye Yigan of the Kudi and Dou Yuni of the Youlian at Taihun River; after defeating them, Tayeigan son of Kudi Qinzhi submitted with his tribe.

sentences.zh: 真等進破侯莫陳部，獲馬牛羊十餘萬頭，追殄遺迸，入大峨谷。

translations.literal: Zhen and others advanced and defeated the Houmochen tribe, obtained horses, cattle, and sheep more than one hundred thousand head, pursued and extinguished scattered remnants, entered Da'e Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhen pressed on, broke the Houmochen, took more than a hundred thousand livestock, pursued the fugitives into Da'e Valley.

sentences.zh: 中山太守仇儒亡匿趙郡，推羣盜趙准為主，號使持節、征西大將軍、冀青二州牧、鉅鹿公，仇儒為准長史，聚黨扇惑。

translations.literal: Zhongshan Administrator Qiu Ru hid in Zhao commandery, pushed bandit Zhao Zhun as lord, styled Envoy Bearing Staff, Grand General Western Campaign, Governors of Ji and Qing, Duke of Julu, Qiu Ru as Zhun's chief clerk, gathered parties and fanned sedition.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Ru, administrator of Zhongshan, hid in Zhao, set up the bandit Zhao Zhun as leader with forged titles, and stirred rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔中領軍長孫肥討平之。

translations.literal: Ordered Central Guard General Zhangsun Fei to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Fei was sent to crush them.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，前清河太守傅世聚黨千餘家，自號撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: former Qinghe Administrator Fu Shi gathered parties of more than a thousand households, styled himself Pacifying the Army General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the former Qinghe administrator Fu Shi raised more than a thousand households and styled himself pacifying army general.

sentences.zh: 五月癸亥，征虜將軍庾岳討破之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day guihai: Pacifying the Barbarians General Yu Yue attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the fifth month Yu Yue defeated him.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，起天華殿。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: began the Tianhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn work began on the Tianhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，大閱于鹿苑，饗賜各有差。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, great review at the deer park; feast rewards each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day he held a great review in the deer park and feasted his officers.

sentences.zh: 陳郡、河南流民萬餘口內徙，遣使者存勞之。

translations.literal: Chen commandery and Henan floating migrants more than ten thousand mouths inwardly relocated; sent envoys to inquire after and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand refugees from Chen and Henan were resettled inland, and envoys were sent to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣眾圍洛陽，司馬德宗將辛恭靖請救。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent masses to besiege Luoyang; Sima Dezong's general Xin Gongjing requested rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing besieged Luoyang; Xin Gongjing of the Jin court begged for aid.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣太尉穆崇率騎六千往赴之。

translations.literal: Eighth month: sent Grand Marshal Mu Chong leading six thousand cavalry to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Mu Chong was sent with six thousand horse to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 增啟京師十二門。

translations.literal: Increased and opened the capital's twelve gates.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve gates of the capital were enlarged and opened.

sentences.zh: 作西武庫。

translations.literal: Built the Western Armory.
translations.idiomatic: The western armory was built.

sentences.zh: 除州郡民租賦之半。

translations.literal: Remitted half the rent and levies of commandery and prefecture people.
translations.idiomatic: Rent and levies were halved throughout the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔禮官備撰眾儀，著于新令。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, ordered ritual officers to prepare and compile the mass of ceremonies, set down in the new statutes.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day he ordered the ritual officers to codify the state ceremonies in the new statutes.

sentences.zh: 范陽人盧溥，聚眾海濱，稱使持節、征北大將軍、幽州刺史，攻掠郡縣，殺幽州刺史封沓干。

translations.literal: Fanyang man Lu Pu gathered masses on the seacoast, styled Envoy Bearing Staff, Grand General Northern Campaign, Regional Inspector of Youzhou, attacked and plundered commanderies and counties, killed Regional Inspector of Youzhou Feng Tagan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Pu of Fanyang gathered a host on the coast, took forged titles as northern campaign general and inspector of Youzhou, raided the districts, and killed the inspector Feng Tagan.

sentences.zh: 慕容盛遼西太守李朗，舉郡內屬。

translations.literal: Murong Sheng's Liaoxi Administrator Li Lang raised the commandery to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lang, Murong Sheng's administrator of Liaoxi, brought his commandery in submission.

sentences.zh: 西河胡帥護諾于、丁零帥翟同、蜀帥韓礱，並相率內附。

translations.literal: Xihe Hu chief Hunuoyu, Dingling chief Zhai Tong, Shu chief Han Long, all together led their tribes to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Hunuoyu of Xihe, Zhai Tong of the Dingling, and Han Long of the Shu each submitted with their tribes.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，太廟成，遷神元、平文、昭成、獻明皇帝神主于太廟。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the Grand Temple completed; moved the Divine Yuan, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming emperors' spirit tablets to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the Grand Temple was completed and the tablets of the Divine Yuan, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming emperors were installed.

sentences.zh: 十有二月甲午，慕容盛征虜將軍、燕郡太守高湖，率戶三千內屬。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jiawu: Murong Sheng's Pacifying the Barbarians General, Administrator of Yan commandery Gao Hu, led three thousand households to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the twelfth month Gao Hu, Sheng's general and administrator of Yan, submitted with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔材官將軍和突討盧溥。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, ordered Material Officers General He Tu to attack Lu Pu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day He Tu was ordered against Lu Pu.

sentences.zh: 天華殿成。

translations.literal: The Tianhua Hall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianhua Hall was completed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，呂光立其子紹為天王，自稱太上皇。

translations.literal: That year, Lü Guang established his son Shao as Heavenly King, styled himself Supreme Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lü Guang made his son Shao heavenly king and took the title of supreme emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 光死，庶子纂殺紹僭立。

translations.literal: Guang died; bastard son Zuan killed Shao and presumptuously established himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang died, his bastard son Zuan murdered Shao and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: [11]禿髮烏孤死，弟鹿孤代立，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: [11] Tufa Wugu died; younger brother Lugu replaced him, sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Tufa Wugu died; his brother Lugu succeeded him and sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月戊午，和突破盧溥於遼西，生獲溥及其子煥，傳送京師，轘之。

translations.literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day wuwu: He Tu defeated Lu Pu at Liaoxi, captured alive Pu and his son Huan, sent in escort to the capital, executed by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the wuwu day of the first month of spring, He Tu defeated Lu Pu in Liaoxi, took him and his son Huan alive, and had them torn apart at the capital.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，有事於北郊。

translations.literal: On day guihai, performed the ceremony at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day he sacrificed at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 分命諸官循行州郡，觀民風俗，察舉不法。

translations.literal: Separately ordered the various offices to tour the provinces, observe the people's customs, inspect and memorialize the unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officials through the provinces to observe customs and report misconduct.

sentences.zh: 賜羣臣布帛各有差。

translations.literal: Bestowed cloth and silk on the host of ministers each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He gave cloth and silk to his ministers according to rank.

sentences.zh: 二月丁亥，詔有司祀日于東郊。

translations.literal: Second month, day dinghai: ordered the relevant offices to sacrifice to the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the second month he ordered sacrifice to the sun at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 始耕籍田。

translations.literal: First plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: He performed the first plowing of the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，皇子聰薨。

translations.literal: On day renyin, the imperial son Cong died.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day the prince Cong died.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，立皇后慕容氏。

translations.literal: Third month, day wuwu: established Empress Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the third month he made Lady Murong empress.

sentences.zh: 是月，穿城南渠通於城內，作東西魚池。

translations.literal: That month, dug the southern city canal communicating within the city, made eastern and western fish ponds.
translations.idiomatic: That month he dug a canal from the south into the city and made fish ponds east and west.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，姚興遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Yao Xing sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Yao Xing sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 五月戊辰，詔謁者僕射張濟使於姚興。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuchen: ordered Master of Guests Zhang Ji as envoy to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the fifth month Zhang Ji was sent as envoy to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 己巳，車駕東巡，遂幸涿鹿，遣使者以太牢祠帝堯、帝舜廟。

translations.literal: On day jisi, the imperial carriage eastern tour, then visited Zhuolu, sent envoys with great sacrifice to sacrifice at the temples of Emperor Yao and Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day he toured east to Zhuolu and sent envoys with great victims to sacrifice at the shrines of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 西幸馬邑，觀灅源。

translations.literal: West to Mayi, viewed the Lei source.
translations.idiomatic: He went west to Mayi to view the Lei springs.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬子，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day renzi: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the seventh month of autumn he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 起中天殿及雲母堂、金華室。

translations.literal: Began the Central Heaven Hall and Mica Hall, Jinhua Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Work began on the Central Heaven Hall, the Mica Hall, and the Jinhua Chamber.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，高車別帥敕力犍，率九百餘落內屬。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Gaoche separate commander Chilejian led more than nine hundred encampments to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Chilejian, a Gaoche sub-chief, submitted with more than nine hundred camps.

sentences.zh: 十有二月乙未，詔曰：「世俗謂漢高起於布衣而有天下，此未達其故也。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day yiwei: an edict said: "The vulgar say Han Gaozu rose from common cloth and possessed all under Heaven — this does not reach the root of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the twelfth month an edict declared: "Common talk holds that Han Gaozu rose from the ranks and won the empire. That misses the point entirely.

sentences.zh: 夫劉承堯統，曠世繼德，有蛇龍之徵，致雲彩之應，五緯上聚，天人俱協，明革命之主，大運所鍾，不可以非望求也。

translations.literal: Liu inherited Yao's succession, virtue spanning ages without break; there were signs of serpent and dragon, responses of clouds and colors; the five planets gathered above, Heaven and man both in accord — a lord of bright revolution, the great fortune belled, cannot be sought by improper hope.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Liu inherited the mandate of Yao. Heaven showed signs in serpent and dragon, clouds and the five planets aligned, and the age itself called for a new ruler. Such a throne is not won by naked ambition.

sentences.zh: 然狂狡之徒，所以顛蹶而不已者，誠惑於逐鹿之說，而迷於天命也。

translations.literal: Yet the mad and cunning, the reason they stumble and fall without end, are truly deluded by the tale of chasing the deer and blind to Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rebels still fall because they believe the old tale that the empire is a deer for anyone to chase, and forget that the mandate belongs to Heaven alone.

sentences.zh: 故有踵覆車之軌，蹈釁逆之蹤，毒甚者傾州郡，害微者敗邑里，至乃身死名頹，殃及九族，從亂隨流，死而不悔，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Therefore there are those who follow the track of overturned carts, tread the traces of treason and rebellion; where poison is severe they overturn provinces and commanderies, where harm is slight they ruin towns and villages; reaching even to body dead and name fallen, calamity reaching the nine clans — following disorder with the current, dying without regret. Is it not painful!
translations.idiomatic: They follow the road of ruined kings, spread rebellion through town and province, destroy themselves and their kin to the ninth degree, and die unrepentant in the flood of disorder. What folly, and what pain!

sentences.zh: 春秋之義，大一統之美，吳楚僭號，久加誅絕，君子賤其偽名，比之塵垢。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals esteems the beauty of great unity; Wu and Chu presumptuously styled themselves and long received execution and extinction; the gentleman despised their false names, comparing them to dust and filth.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals praise unity and condemn usurpation. Wu and Chu took false titles and were destroyed; wise men held their names in contempt, no better than filth.

sentences.zh: 自非繼聖載德，天人合會，帝王之業，夫豈虛應。

translations.literal: Unless one succeeds a sage and bears virtue, Heaven and man unite in meeting — the enterprise of emperor and king, how could it be an empty response?
translations.idiomatic: Unless a man unites heaven and man, succeeds the sages, and bears true virtue, how can imperial rule be anything but an empty pretense?

sentences.zh: 歷觀古今，不義而求非望者，徒喪其保家之道，而伏刀鋸之誅。

translations.literal: Reviewing past and present, those unrighteous who sought improper hope only lost the way to preserve their houses and lay under the punishment of blade and saw.
translations.idiomatic: History shows that every traitor who reached for the throne lost his house and died by the blade.

sentences.zh: 有國有家者，誠能推廢興之有期，審天命之不易，察徵應之潛授，杜競逐之邪言，絕姦雄之僭肆，思多福於止足，則幾於神智矣。

translations.literal: Those with state and family, if they can indeed push away the term of rise and fall, examine that Heaven's mandate is not easy, observe how signs and responses are secretly bestowed, stop the evil words of competing pursuit, cut off the presumptuous license of treacherous heroes, think much of blessing in knowing when to stop — then they are near to divine wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Let every lord weigh the cycle of rise and fall, know that the mandate is not easily held, read the signs Heaven sends, reject the lure of rebellion, and find sufficiency in his station — then he nears wisdom.

sentences.zh: 如此，則可以保榮祿於天年，流餘慶於後世。

translations.literal: Thus one can preserve glory and salary through Heaven's years, flow remaining blessing to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: So may he keep honor through his years and leave blessing to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故禍悖無緣而生，兵甲何因而起？

translations.literal: Being so, then calamity and perversity have no cause to arise, why should arms and armor rise?
translations.idiomatic: Then rebellion finds no foothold, and arms need never be raised.

sentences.zh: 凡厥來世，勗哉戒之，可不慎歟！」

translations.literal: All coming generations, exert yourselves in warning this — can one not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: Let all future ages take warning. Can any man be careless?"

sentences.zh: 時太史屢奏天文錯亂，帝親覽經占，多云改王易政，故數革官號，一欲防塞凶狡，二欲消災應變。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Astrologer repeatedly memorialized that celestial patterns were disordered; the emperor personally viewed the classics of divination; many said change king, change government; therefore he repeatedly changed office titles — first to block and stop the fierce and cunning, second to dispel calamity and respond to change.
translations.idiomatic: The grand astrologer reported disorder in the heavens; the emperor studied the prognostic texts himself, which spoke of change of dynasty. He therefore altered offices again and again, both to thwart traitors and to answer heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 已而慮羣下疑惑，心謗腹非，丙申復詔曰：「上古之治，尚德下名，有任而無爵，易治而事序，故邪謀息而不起，姦慝絕而不作。

translations.literal: Before long, fearing the host below would be doubtful, hearts slandering and bellies dissenting, on day bingshen again an edict said: "The governance of high antiquity esteemed virtue and lowered names; there was appointment but no rank; easy to govern and affairs in order; therefore evil plots ceased and did not arise, treachery and villainy were cut off and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing murmurs among his officers, on the bingshen day he issued another edict: "In high antiquity rulers valued virtue over titles. Offices were duties, not prizes. Evil plots died for want of reward, and treachery found no opening.

sentences.zh: 周姬之末，下凌上替，以號自定，以位制祿，卿世其官，大夫遂事，陽德不暢，議發家陪，故釁由此起，兵由此作。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou of Ji, the lower overawed the upper and replaced them; by title they fixed themselves, by rank they regulated salary; ministers inherited their offices, grandees followed their affairs; yang virtue did not flourish, discussion arose from enriching families — therefore trouble arose from this, arms arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall of Zhou the lower orders overturned their betters, made rank hereditary, and bought office with wealth. Yang virtue failed, families contended for power, and from that came rebellion and war.

sentences.zh: 秦漢之弊，捨德崇侈，能否混雜，賢愚相亂，庶官失序，任非其人。

translations.literal: The defects of Qin and Han abandoned virtue and exalted extravagance; ability and inability mixed together, worthy and foolish confused; the hundred offices lost order, appointment not according to the man.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han abandoned virtue for display, mixed the able with the worthless, and put the wrong men in office.

sentences.zh: 於是忠義之道寢，廉耻之節廢，退讓之風絕，毀譽之議興，莫不由乎貴尚名位，而禍敗及之矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the way of loyalty and righteousness slept, the integrity of shame and honor was abandoned, the wind of yielding withdrew, discussions of ruin and praise arose — all without exception from esteeming and honoring name and rank, while calamity and defeat reached them.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty withered, shame died, modesty vanished, and slander flourished — all because men prized empty titles, and ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 古置三公，職大憂重，故曰『待罪宰相』，將委任責成，非虛寵祿也。

translations.literal: Anciently the Three Excellencies were set; duties great, worries heavy; therefore it is said 'awaiting punishment as chief minister' — intending to entrust responsibility and demand accomplishment, not empty favor and salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies of old bore heavy trust and were called ministers 'awaiting punishment,' not men given empty honor.

sentences.zh: 而今世俗，僉以台輔為榮貴，企慕而求之。

translations.literal: Yet in the present vulgar world, all take terrace and aide as glory and nobility, crane neck and seek them.
translations.idiomatic: Today men crane their necks after the highest offices as if they were glory itself.

sentences.zh: 夫此職司，在人主之所任耳，用之則重，捨之則輕。

translations.literal: These duties and offices rest in the lord of men alone to appoint; using them then they are heavy, discarding them then they are light.
translations.idiomatic: These posts exist only at the sovereign's pleasure; in use they weigh, in disuse they are light.

sentences.zh: 然則官無常名，而任有定分，是則所貴者至矣，何取於鼎司之虛稱也。

translations.literal: Thus offices have no constant name, while duties have fixed allotment — then what is honored reaches the utmost; why take the empty title of chief minister?
translations.idiomatic: Office has no fixed glory; duty has a fixed measure. Honor lies in the work, not in the name of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 夫桀紂之南面，雖高而可薄；

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou facing south — though high yet could be held cheap.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou sat facing south, yet their height deserved contempt.

sentences.zh: 姬旦之為下，雖卑而可尊。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhou in low station — though humble yet could be honored.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou stood low, yet his humility deserved honor.

sentences.zh: 一官可以効智，蓽門可以垂範。

translations.literal: One office can display wisdom; a wicker gate can leave a model.
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom may shine in the lowest post; a wicker gate may leave a model to the age.

sentences.zh: 苟以道德為實，賢於覆餗蔀家矣。

translations.literal: If with morality and virtue as substance, one is worthier than overturned stew and a mat roof.
translations.idiomatic: He who has virtue as his substance is greater than a king in a ruined house.

sentences.zh: 故量己者，令終而義全；

translations.literal: Therefore he who measures himself ends with integrity and righteousness complete.
translations.idiomatic: He who knows his measure dies whole in name and deed.

sentences.zh: 昧利者，身陷而名滅。

translations.literal: He who is blind to profit — body trapped and name extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He who grasps at profit loses body and name together.

sentences.zh: 利之與名，毀譽之疵競；

translations.literal: Profit and name are the competing blemishes of ruin and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Profit and fame breed slander and praise.

sentences.zh: 道之與德，神識之家寶。

translations.literal: The Way and virtue are the family treasure of spirit and knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The Way and virtue are the treasure of the wise.

sentences.zh: 是故道義，治之本；

translations.literal: Therefore the Way and righteousness are the root of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Way and righteousness are the root of rule.

sentences.zh: 名爵，治之末。

translations.literal: Name and rank are the tip of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and ranks are only its branches.

sentences.zh: 名不本於道，不可以為宜；

translations.literal: Name not rooted in the Way cannot be taken as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: A title without the Way is unfit.

sentences.zh: 爵無補於時，不可以為用。

translations.literal: Rank not supplementing the age cannot be taken as useful.
translations.idiomatic: A rank that serves no need is useless.

sentences.zh: 用而不禁，為病深矣。

translations.literal: Using without prohibition — the illness is deep.
translations.idiomatic: To use such men without restraint is a grave sickness.

sentences.zh: 能通其變，不失其正者，其惟聖人乎？

translations.literal: He who can penetrate its changes without losing what is correct — is it not the sage?
translations.idiomatic: Only the sage can change with the times and yet keep to what is right.

sentences.zh: 來者誠思成敗之理，察治亂之由，鑒殷周之失，革秦漢之弊，則幾於治矣。」

translations.literal: Coming generations, truly think on the principle of success and failure, examine the source of order and disorder, mirror the failures of Yin and Zhou, reform the defects of Qin and Han — then one is near to good governance."
translations.idiomatic: Let later ages study success and failure, trace order and chaos to its source, learn from Yin, Zhou, Qin, and Han, and they will be near to good government."

sentences.zh: 是歲，乞伏乾歸為姚興所破，李暠私署涼州牧、涼公。

translations.literal: That year, Qifu Gangui was broken by Yao Xing; Li Gao privately styled Regional Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qifu Gangui was defeated by Yao Xing; Li Gao declared himself inspector of Liangzhou and duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月，高車別帥率其部三千餘落內附。

translations.literal: Year 4, spring, first month: Gaoche separate commander led his division of more than three thousand encampments to submit within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, in the first month of spring, a Gaoche sub-chief submitted with more than three thousand camps.

sentences.zh: 二月丁亥，命樂師入學習舞，釋菜于先聖、先師。

translations.literal: Second month, day dinghai: ordered music masters to enter study dance, release vegetables at the Former Sage and Former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the second month he ordered the music masters trained and performed the vegetable offering before the sage and teacher.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，分命使者循行州郡，聽察辭訟，糾劾不法。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, separately ordered envoys to tour provinces, hear and observe lawsuits, impeach the unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day he sent envoys through the provinces to hear lawsuits and impeach wrongdoers.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝親漁，薦于寢廟。

translations.literal: Third month: the emperor personally fished, offered at the sleeping temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor fished and offered at the sleeping temple.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛卯，罷鄴行臺。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinmao: abolished the Ye traveling secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the fourth month of summer he abolished the traveling secretariat at Ye.

sentences.zh: 詔有司明揚隱逸。

translations.literal: Ordered the relevant offices to clarify and raise the hidden and reclusive.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ministries to seek out hidden worthies.

sentences.zh: 五月，起紫極殿、玄武樓、涼風觀、石池、鹿苑臺。

translations.literal: Fifth month: began the Purple Pole Hall, Black Tortoise Tower, Cool Wind Pavilion, Stone Pool, and Deer Park Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he began the Purple Pole Hall, Black Tortoise Tower, Cool Wind Pavilion, Stone Pool, and Deer Park Terrace.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，詔鎮遠將軍、兗州刺史長孫肥步騎二萬南徇許昌、彭城。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: ordered Pacifying the Distance General, Yanzhou Regional Inspector Zhangsun Fei with twenty thousand foot and horse south along Xuchang and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he sent Zhangsun Fei with twenty thousand men south against Xuchang and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔賜天下鎮戍將士布帛各有差。

translations.literal: Ordered bestowal on garrison officers and soldiers throughout the realm of cloth and silk each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He gave cloth and silk to the garrison troops according to rank.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月辛亥，詔征西大將軍、常山王遵等率眾五萬討破多蘭部帥木易于，材官將軍和突率騎六千襲黜弗、素古延等諸部。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, day xinhai: ordered Western Campaign Grand General, Prince of Changshan Zun and others to lead masses of fifty thousand to attack and defeat Duolan division chief Muyigan; Material Officers General He Tu led six thousand cavalry to raid the Chufu, Suguyan, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the twelfth month of winter Zun with fifty thousand men defeated Muyigan of the Duolan, while He Tu with six thousand horse raided the Chufu and Suguyan tribes.

sentences.zh: 集博士儒生，比眾經文字，義類相從，凡四萬餘字，號曰眾文經。

translations.literal: Gathered erudites and Confucian scholars, compared the masses of classic characters, meanings classified and followed one another, altogether more than forty thousand characters, titled the Collected Culture Classic.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered scholars, standardized the script across the classics, and compiled more than forty thousand characters into the Collected Culture Classic.

sentences.zh: 是歲，慕容盛死，寶弟熙僭立。

translations.literal: That year, Murong Sheng died; Bao's younger brother Xi presumptuously established himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Sheng died and Bao's brother Xi seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 呂光弟子隆殺纂自立。

translations.literal: Lü Guang's younger brother's son Long killed Zuan and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: Long, nephew of Lü Guang, killed Zuan and made himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 盧水胡沮渠蒙遜私署涼州牧、張掖公。

translations.literal: Lushui Hu Juqu Mengxun privately styled Regional Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui Hu declared himself inspector of Liangzhou and duke of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜及李暠並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Mengxun and Li Gao both sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun and Li Gao both sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月丁丑，慕容熙遣將寇遼西，虎威將軍宿沓干等拒戰不利，棄令支而還。

translations.literal: Year 5, spring, first month, day dingchou: Murong Xi sent generals to raid Liaoxi; Tiger Might General Su Tagan and others resisted battle unfavorably, abandoned Lingzhi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on the dingchou day of the first month of spring, Murong Xi raided Liaoxi; Su Tagan was beaten and withdrew from Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 帝聞姚興將寇邊，庚寅，大簡輿徒，詔并州諸軍積穀于平陽之乾壁。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Yao Xing would raid the frontier; on day gengyin, great review of carriage followers; ordered Bingzhou armies to accumulate grain at Ganbi in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yao Xing meant to attack the frontier, on the gengyin day he reviewed the army and ordered grain stored at Ganbi in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 戊子，材官將軍和突破黜弗、素古延等諸部，獲馬三千餘匹，牛羊七萬餘頭。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Material Officers General He Tu defeated the Chufu, Suguyan, and other tribes, obtained more than three thousand horses, more than seventy thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day He Tu defeated the Chufu and Suguyan and took three thousand horses and seventy thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，蠕蠕社崙遣騎救素古延等，和突逆擊破之于山南河曲，獲鎧馬二千餘匹。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, Rouran Shelun sent cavalry to rescue Suguyan and others; He Tu met and attacked them at the southern mountain river bend, obtained armored horses more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day Shelun of the Rouran sent horse to rescue Suguyan; He Tu met and broke them at the river bend south of the mountains and took two thousand armored horses.

sentences.zh: 班師。

translations.literal: Withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賞賜將士各有差。

translations.literal: Rewards for officers and soldiers each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 二月癸丑，征西大將軍、常山王遵等至安定之高平，木易于率數千騎與衞辰、屈丐棄國遁走，追至隴西瓦亭，不及而還。

translations.literal: Second month, day guichou: Western Campaign Grand General, Prince of Changshan Zun and others reached Gaoping in Anding; Muyigan led several thousand horse with Weichen and Qu Fu abandoned the state and fled; pursued to Wating in Longxi, could not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the second month Zun reached Gaoping in Anding. Muyigan fled west with several thousand horse, Weichen, and Qu Fu; pursuit reached Wating in Longxi but failed to overtake them.

sentences.zh: 獲其輜重庫藏，馬四萬餘匹，駱駝、氂牛三千餘頭，牛、羊九萬餘口。

translations.literal: Obtained their baggage, treasuries, more than forty thousand horses, camels and yak more than three thousand head, cattle and sheep more than ninety thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They seized baggage and stores, forty thousand horses, three thousand camels and yaks, and ninety thousand cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 班賜將士各有差。

translations.literal: Distributed rewards to officers and soldiers each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were rewarded by merit.

sentences.zh: 徙其民於京師。

translations.literal: Relocated their people to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Their people were moved to the capital.

sentences.zh: 沙門張翹自號無上王，與丁零鮮于次保聚黨常山之行唐。

translations.literal: Monk Zhang Qiao styled himself Unsurpassed King, with Dingling Xianyu Cibao gathered parties at Xingtang in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhang Qiao styled himself Unsurpassed King and with Cibao of the Dingling raised a host at Xingtang in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，太守樓伏連討斬之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Administrator Lou Fulian attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Administrator Lou Fulian attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 五月，姚興遣其弟安北將軍、義陽公平率眾四萬來侵，平陽乾壁為平所陷。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Yao Xing sent his younger brother Pacifying the North General, Duke of Yiyang Ping leading masses of forty thousand to invade; Pingyang Ganbi was taken by Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yao Xing sent his brother Ping with forty thousand men; Ping took Ganbi at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 六月，治兵于東郊，部分眾軍，詔鎮西大將軍毗陵王順、長孫肥等三將六萬騎為前鋒。

translations.literal: Sixth month: drilled troops at the eastern suburb, assigned the host of armies; ordered Pacifying the West Grand General Prince of Piling Shun, Zhangsun Fei, and three other generals with sixty thousand cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he reviewed the army at the eastern suburb and named Prince Shun of Piling, Zhangsun Fei, and two other generals to lead sixty thousand horse as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊辰朔，車駕西討。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day wuchen on the new moon: the imperial carriage western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the seventh month of autumn, the wuchen day, the court marched west.

sentences.zh: 八月乙巳，至於柴壁，平固守，進軍圍之，姚興悉舉其眾來救。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yisi: reached Chaibi; Ping firmly defended; advanced army and besieged it; Yao Xing raised his entire host to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the eighth month he reached Chaibi, invested Ping's stronghold, and Yao Xing came with his whole army.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝渡蒙坑，逆擊興軍，大破之。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, the emperor crossed Meng Ravine, met and attacked Xing's army, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day he crossed Meng Ravine, met Xing's army, and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，平赴水而死，俘其餘眾三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Ping went to the water and died; captured the remaining masses more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Ping drowned; more than thirty thousand of his men were taken.

sentences.zh: 語在興傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 獲興征虜將軍、尚書右僕射狄伯支，越騎校尉唐小方，積弩將軍姚梁國，建忠將軍雷星、康官，[12]北中郎將康猥，平從弟伯禽已下、四品將軍已上四十餘人。

translations.literal: Captured Xing's Pacifying the Barbarians General, Secretariat Right Vice Director Di Bozhi, Rapid-as-Horses Commandant Tang Xiaofang, Strong Crossbow General Yao Liangguo, Establishing Loyalty General Lei Xing, Kang Guan, [12] Northern Gentlemen General Kang Wei, Ping's younger brother's son Bohun and below, fourth-rank generals and above more than forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: He took Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, Yao Liangguo, Lei Xing, Kang Guan, [12] Kang Wei, Bohun nephew of Ping, and more than forty officers of fourth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 獲先亡臣王次多、靳懃，並斬以徇。

translations.literal: Captured former lost ministers Wang Ciduo, Jin Qin, all beheaded and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized the defectors Wang Ciduo and Jin Qin and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 興頻使請和，帝不許。

translations.literal: Xing repeatedly sent envoys seeking peace; the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Xing sued repeatedly for peace; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 羣臣勸進平蒲坂，帝慮蠕蠕為難，戊申，班師。

translations.literal: The host of ministers urged advancing to pacify Puban; the emperor feared the Rouran would make trouble; on day wushen, withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers urged him on to Puban, but fearing the Rouran he withdrew on the wushen day.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，車駕次晉陽。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: the imperial carriage halted at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court halted at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 徵相州刺史庾岳為司空。

translations.literal: Summoned Yanzhou Regional Inspector Yu Yue as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue, inspector of Yanzhou, was summoned to be minister of works.

sentences.zh: 遣左將軍莫題討上黨羣盜秦頗、丁零翟都於壺關。

translations.literal: Sent Left General Mo Ti to attack Shangdang bandits Qin Po, Dingling Zhai Du at Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Ti was sent against the bandits Qin Po and Zhai Du of the Dingling at Huguan.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，上黨太守捕頗，斬之，都走林慮。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Shangdang Administrator captured Po and beheaded him; Du fled to Linyu.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day the administrator of Shangdang captured and killed Po; Du fled to Linyu.

sentences.zh: 十有二月辛亥，至自西征。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day xinhai: returned from the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the twelfth month he returned from the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕社崙犯塞，詔常山王遵追之，不及而還。

translations.literal: Rouran Shelun violated the frontier; ordered Prince of Changshan Zun to pursue, could not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shelun of the Rouran raided the frontier; Zun pursued but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 越勤莫弗率其部萬餘家內屬，居五原之北。

translations.literal: Yueqin Mofu led his division of more than ten thousand households to submit within the borders, dwelling north of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yueqin Mofu submitted with more than ten thousand households and was settled north of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，禿髮鹿孤病死，弟傉檀統任，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year, Tufa Lugu died of illness; younger brother Rutan took overall charge, sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tufa Lugu died; his brother Rutan succeeded him and sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月辛未，朔方尉遲部別帥率萬餘家內屬，入居雲中。

translations.literal: Year 6, spring, first month, day xinwei: Shuofang Yuchi division separate commander led more than ten thousand households to submit within the borders, entering to dwell in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on the xinwei day of the first month of spring, a Yuchi sub-chief of Shuofang submitted with more than ten thousand households and was settled in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，大簡輿徒，將略江淮，平荊揚之亂。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: great review of carriage followers, intending to strike the Jiang and Huai, pacify the disorder of Jing and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he reviewed the army, intending to march on the Jiang and Huai and pacify the south.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，鎮西大將軍、司隸校尉、毗陵王順有罪，以王還第。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Pacifying the West Grand General, Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Piling Shun had crime, demoted to prince and returned to his estate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Prince Shun of Piling was found guilty, stripped of office, and sent to his estate.

sentences.zh: 戊子，車駕北巡，築離宮于犲山，縱士校獵，東北踰罽嶺，出參合、代谷。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, the imperial carriage northern tour, built a detached palace at Chai Mountain, released soldiers to hunt in competition, northeast crossed Gui Ridge, exited Canhe and Dai valleys.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day he toured north, built a lodge on Chai Mountain, held a great hunt, crossed Gui Ridge northeast, and passed through Canhe and Dai.

sentences.zh: 九月，行幸南平城，規度灅南，面夏屋山，背黃瓜堆，將建新邑。

translations.literal: Ninth month: traveled to Nanping City, planned the south of Lei, faced Xiawu Mountain, backed on Huangguadui, intending to build a new city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he went to Nanping, surveyed the country south of Lei below Xiawu Mountain and Huangguadui, and planned a new capital.

sentences.zh: 辛未，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，起西昭陽殿。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: began the Western Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he began the Western Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，立皇子嗣為齊王，加車騎大將軍，位相國；

translations.literal: On day yimao, established the imperial son Si as Prince of Qi, added General of Chariots and Cavalry, rank equal to the prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day he made the prince Si prince of Qi, general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in rank to the prime minister.

sentences.zh: 紹為清河王，加征南大將軍；

translations.literal: Shao as Prince of Qinghe, added Grand General Southern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was made prince of Qinghe and grand general southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 熙為陽平王；

translations.literal: Xi as Prince of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was made prince of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 曜為河南王。

translations.literal: Yao as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was made prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 封故秦慜王子夔為豫章王，陳留王子右將軍悅為朱提王。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed former Prince of Qin Min's son Kui as Prince of Yuzhang, Chenliu Prince's son Right General Yue as Prince of Zhuti.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, son of the former Prince Min of Qin, was made prince of Yuzhang; Yue, son of the prince of Chenliu, was made prince of Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔將軍伊謂率騎二萬北襲高車。

translations.literal: On day dingsi, ordered General Yi Wei to lead twenty thousand cavalry north to raid the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day Yi Wei was ordered north with twenty thousand horse against the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 司馬德宗遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Sima Dezong sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Dezong sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 十有一月庚午，伊謂大破高車。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day gengwu: Yi Wei greatly defeated the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the eleventh month Yi Wei routed the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 是年，島夷桓玄廢其主司馬德宗而自立，僭稱大楚。

translations.literal: That year, the island barbarian Huan Xuan deposed his lord Sima Dezong and established himself, presumptuously styled Great Chu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Huan Xuan of the eastern isles deposed Sima Dezong and declared himself emperor of Great Chu.

sentences.zh: 天賜元年春正月，遣離石護軍劉託率騎三千襲蒲子。

translations.literal: Tianci year 1, spring, first month: sent Lishi Protecting Army Liu Tuo leading three thousand cavalry to raid Puzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianci, in the first month of spring, Liu Tuo was sent with three thousand horse to raid Puzi.

sentences.zh: 三月丙寅，擒姚興寧北將軍、泰平太守衡譚，獲三千餘口。

translations.literal: Third month, day bingyin: captured Yao Xing's Pacifying the North General, Taiping Administrator Heng Tan, obtained more than three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the third month he took Heng Tan, Xing's pacifying-the-north general and administrator of Taiping, with more than three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 初限縣戶不滿百罷之。

translations.literal: At first limited: counties with households not filling one hundred were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At first he abolished any county with fewer than a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，詔尚書郎中公孫表使於江南，以觀桓玄之釁也。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: ordered Secretariat Gentleman Gongsun Biao as envoy to the lands south of the Yangtze, to observe Huan Xuan's signs of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he sent Gongsun Biao of the Secretariat to the south to watch Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 值玄敗而還。

translations.literal: Encountered Xuan's defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived as Xuan fell and returned.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕社崙從弟悅伐大那等謀殺社崙而立大那。

translations.literal: Rouran Shelun's younger cousin Yue attacked Dana and others, plotting to kill Shelun and establish Dana.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Shelun's cousin among the Rouran, plotted with Dana and others to kill Shelun and set Dana up in his place.

sentences.zh: 發覺，來奔。

translations.literal: The plot was discovered; they came fleeing in submission.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered and they fled to submit.

sentences.zh: 五月，置山東諸冶，發州郡徒謫造兵甲。

translations.literal: Fifth month: established smelteries east of the mountains, mobilized convicts and exiles from provinces and commanderies to forge arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he set up smelteries in the east and drafted convicts from the provinces to forge arms.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，帝臨昭陽殿，分置眾職，引朝臣文武，親自簡擇，量能叙用；

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month: the emperor attended Zhaoyang Hall, separately set the host of offices, summoned civil and military court ministers, personally selected them, measured ability and appointed use.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn he held court at Zhaoyang Hall, reorganized the bureaucracy, and personally chose men for office according to their talents.

sentences.zh: 制爵四等，曰「王、公、侯、子」，除伯、男之號；

translations.literal: Established four noble ranks, saying "king, duke, marquis, viscount," abolishing the titles of earl and baron.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed four noble ranks — king, duke, marquis, and viscount — and abolished the ranks of earl and baron.

sentences.zh: 追錄舊臣，加以封爵，各有差。

translations.literal: Posthumously recorded old ministers, adding enfeoffments and ranks, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored old ministers with titles and ranks according to merit.

sentences.zh: 是秋，江南大亂，流民繈負而奔淮北，行道相尋。

translations.literal: That autumn, great disorder in the lands south of the Yangtze; floating migrants swaddled on back fled to north of the Huai; on the road one followed another.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the south fell into chaos, and refugees swarmed north across the Huai in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛巳，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day xinsi: great amnesty, changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the tenth month of winter he proclaimed a general amnesty and a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 築西宮。

translations.literal: Built the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，上幸西宮，大選朝臣，令各辨宗黨，保舉才行，諸部子孫失業賜爵者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: the emperor visited the Western Palace, great selection of court ministers, ordered each to distinguish his clan lineage, guarantee and recommend talent and conduct; sons and grandsons of various divisions who had lost livelihood were granted ranks, more than two thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he went to the Western Palace, ordered the court to sort clans and recommend talent, and ennobled more than two thousand men of the tribal nobility who had fallen on hard times.

sentences.zh: 十有二月戊辰，車駕幸犲山宮。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day wuchen: the imperial carriage visited Chai Mountain Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the twelfth month the court visited Chai Mountain Palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，島夷劉裕起兵誅桓玄。

translations.literal: That year, the island barbarian Liu Yu raised troops and executed Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Yu of the eastern isles rose and killed Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月癸亥，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Year 2, spring, second month, day guihai: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the guihai day of the second month of spring, the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，車駕有事于西郊，車旗盡黑。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: the imperial carriage performed the ceremony at the western suburb; carriage banners all black.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he sacrificed at the western suburb with all banners black.

sentences.zh: 是歲，司馬德宗復僭立。

translations.literal: That year, Sima Dezong again presumptuously established himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Dezong again took the throne.

sentences.zh: 慕容德死，兄子超僭立。

translations.literal: Murong De died; elder brother's son Chao presumptuously established himself.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De died and his nephew Chao seized power.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月甲申，車駕北巡，幸犲山宮。

translations.literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day jiashen: the imperial carriage northern tour, visited Chai Mountain Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the jiashen day of the first month of spring, the court toured north to Chai Mountain Palace.

sentences.zh: 校獵，至屋孤山。

translations.literal: Conducted a hunt, reaching Wugu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted as far as Wugu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 二月乙亥，幸代園山，建五石亭。

translations.literal: Second month, day yihai: visited Dai Garden Mountain, built the Five Stone Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the second month he went to Dai Garden Mountain and built the Five Stone Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Third month, day gengzi: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the third month he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚申，復幸犲山宮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengshen: again visited Chai Mountain Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the fourth month of summer he again went to Chai Mountain Palace.

sentences.zh: 占授著作郎王宜弟造兵法孤虛立成圖三百六十時。

translations.literal: Bestowed appointment on Editorial Director Wang Yidi to make the military classic Guxu Licheng Diagram of three hundred sixty seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the editorial director Wang Yidi to compile a three-hundred-and-sixty-part treatise on military formations.

sentences.zh: 遂登定襄角史山，又幸馬城。

translations.literal: Thereupon ascended Dingxiang Jiaoshi Mountain, again visited Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then climbed Jiaoshi Mountain in Dingxiang and went on to Macheng.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On day jiawu, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是月，蠕蠕寇邊，夜召兵，將旦，賊走，乃罷。

translations.literal: That month, the Rouran raided the frontier; at night troops were summoned; at dawn the bandits fled; then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Rouran raided the border; troops were called up by night, but the enemy fled by dawn and the alarm was stood down.

sentences.zh: 六月，發八部五百里內男丁築灅南宮，門闕高十餘丈；

translations.literal: Sixth month: mobilized men from the eight divisions within five hundred li to build the Leinan Palace; gate towers more than ten zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he drafted men from the eight divisions within five hundred li to build the Leinan Palace, with gate towers more than ten zhang high.

sentences.zh: 引溝穿池，廣苑囿；

translations.literal: Led canals and dug pools, broadened parks and preserves.
translations.idiomatic: Canals were dug and the parks enlarged.

sentences.zh: 規立外城，方二十里，分置市里，經塗洞達。

translations.literal: Planned to establish an outer city, twenty li square, separately set wards and markets, main roads penetrating through.
translations.idiomatic: He planned an outer city twenty li square, with wards, markets, and thoroughfares.

sentences.zh: 三十日罷。

translations.literal: Thirty days and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The work was halted after thirty days.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，太尉穆崇薨。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Grand Marshal Mu Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Mu Chong died.

sentences.zh: 八月甲辰，行幸犲山宮，遂至青牛山。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jiachen: traveled to Chai Mountain Palace, then reached Blue Ox Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the eighth month he went to Chai Mountain Palace and on to Blue Ox Mountain.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，西登武要北原，觀九十九泉，造石亭，遂之石漠。

translations.literal: On day bingchen, west ascended Wuyao North Plain, viewed the ninety-nine springs, built a stone pavilion, then went to the stone desert.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day he climbed the Wuyao north plain, viewed the ninety-nine springs, built a stone pavilion, and entered the stone desert.

sentences.zh: 九月甲戌朔，幸漠南鹽池。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jiaxu on the new moon: visited the salt pool south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the ninth month, the jiaxu day, he visited the salt pool south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 壬午，至漠中，觀天鹽池；

translations.literal: On day renwu, reached the center of the desert, viewed the heavenly salt pool.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day he reached the heart of the desert and viewed the heavenly salt pool.

sentences.zh: 度漠，北之吐鹽池。

translations.literal: Crossed the desert, north to the Tu salt pool.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the desert north to the Tu salt pool.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，南還長川。

translations.literal: On day guisi, returned south to Changchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day he turned south to Changchuan.

sentences.zh: 丙申，臨觀長陂。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, overlooked Chang Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day he overlooked Chang Marsh.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚申，車駕還宮。
