translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the tenth month of winter he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 四年春二月，封皇子脩為河間王，處文為長樂王，連為廣平王，黎為京兆王。

translations.literal: Year 4, spring, second month: enfeoffed the imperial son Xiu as Prince of Hejian, Chuwen as Prince of Changle, Lian as Prince of Guangping, Li as Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, in the second month of spring, he enfeoffed Xiu as prince of Hejian, Chuwen as prince of Changle, Lian as prince of Guangping, and Li as prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，北巡。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he toured the north.

sentences.zh: 自參合陂東過蟠羊山，大雨，暴水流輜重數百乘，殺百餘人。

translations.literal: From Canhe Marsh east past Panyang Mountain, great rain, sudden water carried off several hundred baggage wagons, killed more than a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: East from Canhe Marsh past Panyang Mountain a cloudburst swept away hundreds of wagons and killed more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 遂東北踰石漠，至長川，幸濡源。

translations.literal: Thereupon northeast crossed the stone desert, reached Changchuan, visited Ruyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the stone desert northeast to Changchuan and went on to Ruyuan.

sentences.zh: 常山王遵有罪賜死。

translations.literal: Prince of Changshan Zun had crime and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zun of Changshan was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，車駕自濡源西幸參合陂。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage from Ruyuan west visited Canhe Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he went west from Ruyuan to Canhe Marsh.

sentences.zh: 築北宮垣，三旬而罷，乃還宮。

translations.literal: Built the north palace wall; thirty days and stopped; then returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He built the north palace wall in thirty days, then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 八月，幸犲山宮。

translations.literal: Eighth month: visited Chai Mountain Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he went to Chai Mountain Palace.

sentences.zh: 是月，誅司空庾岳。

translations.literal: That month, executed Minister of Works Yu Yue.
translations.idiomatic: That month he executed Yu Yue, minister of works.

sentences.zh: 冬十有一月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，慕容寶養子高雲殺熙自立，赫連屈丐自稱大單于、大夏天王。

translations.literal: That year, Murong Bao's adopted son Gao Yun killed Xi and established himself; Helian Qu Fu styled himself Great Chanyu, Great King of Summer.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gao Yun, Bao's adopted son, killed Xi and seized the throne; Helian Qu Fu declared himself Great Chanyu and Great King of Summer.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，行幸犲山宮，遂如參合陂，觀漁於延水，[13]至寧川。

translations.literal: Year 5, spring, first month: traveled to Chai Mountain Palace, then to Canhe Marsh, viewed fishing on the Yan River, [13] reaching Ningchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, in the first month of spring, he went to Chai Mountain Palace and Canhe Marsh, fished on the Yan River, [13] and reached Ningchuan.

sentences.zh: 三月，姚興遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Third month: Yao Xing sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yao Xing sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 是歲，皇孫燾生。

translations.literal: That year, the imperial grandson Tao was born.
translations.idiomatic: That year the imperial grandson Tao was born.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，帝不豫。

translations.literal: Year 6, summer: the emperor was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, in summer, the emperor fell ill.

sentences.zh: 初，帝服寒食散，自太醫令陰羌死後，藥數動發，至此逾甚。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor took cold-food powder; from after Medical Director Yin Qiang died, the medicine several times stirred outbreaks, reaching here ever more severe.
translations.idiomatic: He had long taken cold-food powder; after the medical director Yin Qiang died the doses brought on ever fiercer attacks.

sentences.zh: 而災變屢見，憂懣不安，或數日不食，或不寢達旦。

translations.literal: Yet calamities and anomalies repeatedly appeared; worried and vexed, ill at ease; sometimes several days without eating, sometimes not sleeping until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Omens multiplied, his mind grew troubled, and he would go days without food or sleep until dawn.

sentences.zh: 歸咎羣下，喜怒乖常，謂百僚左右人不可信，慮如天文之占，或有肘腋之虞。

translations.literal: He blamed the host below; joy and anger contrary to constant; said the hundred officials and attendants left and right were not to be trusted; feared as in the astronomical prognostication, there might be trouble at the elbow and armpit.
translations.idiomatic: He turned on his ministers, raged without cause, and trusted no one around him, fearing the court prognostications of treason at his side.

sentences.zh: 追思既往成敗得失，終日竟夜獨語不止，若旁有鬼物對揚者。

translations.literal: Recalling past success and failure, gain and loss, all day and night alone he spoke without stopping, as if ghostly things beside him answered and responded.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded over past victories and defeats, talking to himself day and night as though ghosts answered back.

sentences.zh: 朝臣至前，追其舊惡皆見殺害，其餘或以顏色變動，或以喘息不調，或以行步乖節，或以言辭失措，帝皆以為懷惡在心，變見於外，乃手自毆擊，死者皆陳天安殿前。

translations.literal: Court ministers who came before him — he pursued their old wrongs and all were killed; the rest, whether facial color changed, or breath not regulated, or gait not in measure, or speech and deportment in error — the emperor all considered that malice was in the heart and change appeared outside; then personally beat and struck them; the dead were all displayed before Tian'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who came before him were killed for old grudges, or for a changed expression, uneven breathing, awkward step, or a slip of the tongue. He beat them to death himself and had the bodies displayed before Tian'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 於是朝野人情各懷危懼，有司懈怠，莫相督攝，百工偷劫，盜賊公行，巷里之間人為希少。

translations.literal: Thereupon court and countryside, people's feelings each harbored peril and fear; responsible offices were slack, none mutually supervised and urged; the hundred crafts stole and plundered; bandits and thieves walked openly; between lanes and alleys people were few.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country lived in terror. Officials neglected their duties, craftsmen looted, and thieves walked openly until the streets were nearly empty.

sentences.zh: 帝亦聞之，曰：「朕縱之使然，待過災年，當更清治之爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor also heard of it and said: "I let it become so; wait until the disaster year passes, and I shall again clear and govern it.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of it he said, "I brought this on myself. After the bad year passes I will set things right again."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，慕容支屬百餘家，謀欲外奔，發覺，伏誅，死者三百餘人。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Murong branch families more than a hundred households plotted to flee outward; discovered; executed in secret; dead numbered more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn more than a hundred Murong households plotted to flee; the plot was discovered and more than three hundred were executed.

sentences.zh: 八月，衞王儀謀叛，賜死。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Prince of Wei Yi plotted rebellion, granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Prince Yi of Wei plotted treason and was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊辰，帝崩於天安殿，時年三十九。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuchen: the emperor died at Tian'an Hall; at the time age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the tenth month of winter he died in Tian'an Hall at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 永興二年九月甲寅，上諡宣武皇帝，葬於盛樂金陵，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: Yongxing year 2, ninth month, day jiayin: posthumous title Emperor Xuanwu, buried at Shengle Jinling, temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxing, on the jiayin day of the ninth month, he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xuanwu, buried at Jinling in Shengle, with temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: [14]泰常五年，改諡曰道武。

translations.literal: [14] Taichang year 5, changed posthumous title to Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: [14] In the fifth year of Taichang his posthumous title was changed to Daowu.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉氏崩離，戎羯乘釁，僭偽紛糾，犲狼競馳。

translations.literal: The historian says: The house of Jin collapsed and parted; Rong and Jie rode the opportunity; presumptuous and false tangled in confusion; jackals and wolves competed in the chase.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When the house of Jin fell apart, the barbarians seized their chance; pretenders multiplied and wolves competed for the prey.

sentences.zh: 太祖顯晦安危之中，屈伸潛躍之際，驅率遺黎，奮其靈武，克剪方難，遂啟中原，朝拱人神，顯登皇極。

translations.literal: Taizu, within showing and hiding, safety and peril, bending and stretching, lurking and leaping, drove and led the remnant masses, roused their spirit and martial power, was able to cut down regional difficulties, then opened the central land, court bowed to man and spirit, clearly ascended the imperial pole.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, through danger and concealment, roused the remnant peoples, swept away his rivals, opened the central plains, and took the throne in truth.

sentences.zh: 雖冠履不暇，栖遑外土，而制作經謨，咸存長世。

translations.literal: Though cap and shoes had no leisure, he dwelled in haste on outer soil, yet institutions, standards, and plans all endured for long generations.
translations.idiomatic: Though he wandered long in exile, the institutions he founded endured for generations.

sentences.zh: 所謂大人利見，百姓與能，抑不世之神武也。

translations.literal: What is called the great man's favorable seeing, the hundred people sharing in his power — perhaps suppressing unworldly spirit and martialness.
translations.idiomatic: Truly he was the great man of the Changes, the ruler the people could follow — a martial spirit not of this world.

sentences.zh: 而屯厄有期，禍生非慮，將人事不足，豈天實為之。

translations.literal: Yet hardship and obstruction had their term; calamity arose beyond calculation — will it be that human affairs were insufficient, or did Heaven truly do it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet his term was cut short and disaster came unlooked for — was it only human failure, or did Heaven itself decree it?

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

translations.idiomatic: On "Liu Xian's brother Feini": the Northern, Ji, Dian, and Ju editions read "Kangni"; the Baibaina and Nan editions read "Feini."

translations.idiomatic: Below and in Liu Xian's biography (j. 23) the brother is called Kangni or Kanglei, not Feini.

translations.idiomatic: Kangni therefore seems correct.

translations.literal: Kumo division chief Jiuji left behind the scattered: Northern History volume 1 has the character Xi after "Kumo."
translations.idiomatic: On "Kumo chief Jiuji": Northern History 1 inserts Xi after Kumo.

translations.idiomatic: The tribe is Kumo Xi, or simply Xi — not Kumo alone; Xi has probably dropped out here.

translations.idiomatic: At Taihe compound surnames were reduced to single characters, usually homophones from the old form — further evidence that Chigan is Xuegan.

sentences.zh: 史傳所載姓叱干的人除個別例子外都作「叱干」，金石萃編卷九六、八瓊室金石補正卷六三載唐資州刺史叱干公三教道場文，更為顯證。

translations.idiomatic: Historical sources normally write the name as Chigan; the Tang inscription of Inspector Chigan Gong in Jinshi cuibian 96 and Babao shi jinshi buzheng 63 is still clearer proof.

sentences.zh: 〈一一〉
封拜公侯將軍刺史太守尚書郎已下悉用文人 諸本「封」下無「拜」字，北史卷一有。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed marquises and dukes, generals, regional inspectors, administrators; Secretariat gentlemen and below all used literary men: all editions lack "enfeoff" below "enfeoff," Northern History juan 1 has it.
translations.idiomatic: On "enfeoffed nobles and all used literary men": the editions omit bai (appoint) after feng (enfeoff); Northern History 1 has it.

sentences.zh: 按將軍以下官不得云「封」，若「將軍、刺史、太守」連下「尚書郎已下」讀，則是將軍也悉用文人，更誤。

translations.literal: According to generals and below, offices cannot be said "enfeoff"; if "generals, regional inspectors, administrators" are read continuously with "Secretariat gentlemen and below," then generals also all used literary men — further error.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and magistrates are appointed, not enfeoffed; without bai, the text would make even generals "literary men" by misreading the list.

sentences.zh: 知這裏脫「拜」字，今據補。

translations.literal: Knowing here the character "appoint" is missing, now supplemented according to the evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The word bai has dropped out; it is restored here.

sentences.zh: 徙山東六州民吏及徒何高麗雜夷三十六萬百工伎巧十萬餘口以充京師 北史卷一、冊府卷四八六

translations.literal: Relocated people, officials, and clerks of six provinces east of the mountains and Tujie, Gaoli, various Yi thirty-six myriads, artisans and craftsmen more than one hundred thousand mouths to fill the capital: Northern History juan 1, Cefu juan 486
translations.idiomatic: On relocating 360,000 families and 100,000 artisans to the capital: Northern History 1 and Cefu 486

sentences.zh: 〈五八一八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 5818〉

sentences.zh: 「三十六萬」作「三十六署」。

translations.literal: read "thirty-six offices" for "thirty-six myriads."
translations.idiomatic: read "thirty-six offices" for "thirty-six myriads."

sentences.zh: 按通鑑卷一一０

translations.literal: According to Zizhi Tongjian juan 110
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian 110

sentences.zh: 〈三四六三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3463〉

sentences.zh: 此條作「徙山東六州吏民、雜夷十餘萬口以實代」，以十餘萬口為這次遷徙的總口數。

translations.literal: this entry reads "relocated people and officials of six provinces east of the mountains, various Yi more than one hundred thousand mouths to fill Dai," taking more than one hundred thousand mouths as the total mouths of this relocation.
translations.idiomatic: gives the total as "more than 100,000 mouths" for the whole relocation.

sentences.zh: 若「署」字作「萬」，則合計當云「四十餘萬口」，似司馬光所見魏書也作「三十六署」。

translations.literal: If the character "office" were read as "myriad," then the total should say "more than four hundred thousand mouths" — it seems the Wei shu Sima Guang saw also read "thirty-six offices."
translations.idiomatic: If wan (myriad) were correct the total would be 400,000+, so Sima Guang's Wei shu probably had shu (office).

sentences.zh: 「署」是百工伎巧所屬的機構。

translations.literal: "Office" is the institution to which artisans and craftsmen belonged.
translations.idiomatic: Shu denotes the workshops to which the artisans belonged.

sentences.zh: 南、北朝少府及太府管轄的官府手工業作坊多設置「署」，隋書百官志記梁少府所屬有十五署，北齊太府所屬有十三署，若再加上太常、光祿、將作所屬，這種「署」是很多的。

translations.literal: Southern and Northern dynasties: the Court of the Imperial Treasury and Grand Court supervised government handicraft workshops mostly setting up "offices"; Suishu Offices Treatise records Liang Court of the Imperial Treasury subordinate to fifteen offices, Northern Qi Grand Court subordinate to thirteen offices; if adding Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Directorate of Imperial Works, such "offices" were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Northern and Southern dynasties workshops were organized as shu under the treasury ministries; Liang had fifteen, Northern Qi thirteen, and more under other ministries.

sentences.zh: 「三十六署」或是後燕所置署數，或一般泛稱。

translations.literal: "Thirty-six offices" may be offices set by Later Yan, or a general designation.
translations.idiomatic: "Thirty-six offices" may be Later Yan's count or a general term.

sentences.zh: 這裏「萬」當是「署」字之訛。

translations.literal: Here "myriad" is probably a corruption of the character "office."
translations.idiomatic: Here wan (myriad) is probably a corruption of shu (office).

sentences.zh: 諸華乏主 諸本「乏」訛「之」，今據御覽卷一０一

translations.literal: The various Hu lacked a lord: all editions corrupt "lacked" to "of," now corrected according to Imperial Readings juan 101
translations.idiomatic: On "the various Hu lacked a lord": editions wrongly read zhi (of) for fa (lacked); corrected from Imperial Readings 101

translations.literal: , Cefu juan 6
translations.idiomatic: , Cefu 6

translations.literal: 〈page 65〉

sentences.zh: 改正。

translations.literal: corrected.
translations.idiomatic: and Cefu 6.

sentences.zh: 庶子纂殺紹僭立 百衲本、南本「庶子」作「太子」，北、汲、殿、局四本作「庶子」。

translations.literal: Bastard son Zuan killed Shao and presumptuously established himself: Baibaina and Nan editions read "crown prince" for "bastard son"; Northern, Ji, Dian, and Ju four editions read "bastard son."
translations.idiomatic: On "bastard son Zuan killed Shao": Baibaina and Nan read "crown prince"; Northern, Ji, Dian, and Ju read "bastard son."

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷一二二呂光載記，呂光的太子即紹，纂乃光庶長子。

translations.literal: According to Account of Lü Guang in Jinshu juan 122, Lü Guang's crown prince was Shao; Zuan was Guang's eldest bastard son.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu 122, Account of Lü Guang, makes Shao the crown prince and Zuan Guang's eldest bastard son.

sentences.zh: 今從北本以下諸本。

translations.literal: Now follow Northern edition and editions below.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern-group reading is adopted.

sentences.zh: 康官 按晉書卷一一八姚興載記下兩見都作「康宦」，疑「官」字形近而訛，但本書卷一０五姚興傳亦作「康官」，今不改。

translations.literal: Kang Guan: according to Account of Yao Xing below in Jinshu juan 118, both occurrences read "Kang Huan"; suspect "Guan" is corruption from similar form, but Yao Xing biography in this book juan 105 also reads "Kang Guan" — now not changed.
translations.idiomatic: On "Kang Guan": Jinshu 118 twice has Kang Huan, but j. 105 of this book also has Guan — left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 觀漁於延水 北史卷一「於」作「于」。

translations.literal: Viewed fishing on the Yan River: Northern History juan 1 reads "at" as "yu."
translations.idiomatic: On "fishing on the Yan River": Northern History 1 writes yu for yu (at/on).

sentences.zh: 按「于延」是水名，見漢書卷二八地理志下代郡且如縣，字當作「于」，但水經注卷一三灅水篇亦「于延」「於延」雜見，今不改。

translations.literal: According to "Yuyan" is a river name, seen in Hanshu Geography Treatise lower Dai commandery Qieyu county; the character should be written "yu," but Shuijingzhu juan 13 Lei River section also has "yuyan" and "yuyan" mixed — now not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyan is a river name in Hanshu 28; the form yu is correct, though Shuijingzhu 13 mixes yu and yu — left unchanged.

translations.literal: Yongxing year 2, ninth month
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing year 2, ninth month

translations.idiomatic: (to)

sentences.zh: 廟號太祖 按永興二年

translations.literal: temple name Taizu: according to Yongxing year 2
translations.idiomatic: On "temple name Taizu": in Yongxing year 2

sentences.zh: 〈四一０〉
上拓跋珪的廟號是「烈祖」，至太和十五年

translations.literal: Tuoba Gui's temple name was "Liezu"; only at Taihe year 15
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui's temple name was Liezu; only in Taihe year 15

sentences.zh: 〈四九一〉
才改「太祖」，見本書卷八四孫惠蔚傳及卷一０八禮志。

translations.literal: was it changed to "Taizu," see Sun Huiwei biography and Rites Treatise in this book juan 84 and juan 108.
translations.idiomatic: was it changed to Taizu, as in Sun Huiwei's biography, j. 84, and the Rites Treatise, j. 108.

sentences.zh: 這裏「太祖」乃「烈祖」之誤。

translations.literal: Here "Taizu" is an error for "Liezu."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu here should read Liezu.
